core-admin-overview.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

You run the screens under Administration in the side menu. This map lists each screen, what it controls and who else notices when you change it.

The admin map

Screen in the side menu What it controls Who else it affects Help page
Users Who can sign in to the Hub, and which roles they hold. The person you change. Deactivating signs them out at once; a role you take away stops working at once. Users
Calendar access Each person's Calendar role and ministries. The person you change, within a minute. Calendar administrators and Calendar system administrators use this screen too, with limits that don't apply to you. Calendar access
Organizations Ministries: names, ministers, contacts, page links, abbreviations, HQ and public settings, deactivation and hand-over. The public site's ministry pages, subscribers, Calendar users, release editors. Site editors can edit ministry details here too. Organizations
Organizations > Cabinet change A new cabinet's renames, new ministries and hand-overs, published together. Everyone who uses a ministry: the public site, subscribers, staff, the Calendar, draft releases. Cabinet change
Government terms The dates of each government term. The public archive, which lists releases by term. Government terms
Sectors, themes and tags The sector, theme and tag lists. The public site, the subscribe page and the release editor, within a minute. Sectors, themes and tags
Release page titles The page titles a new release can choose, such as News Release. Release editors creating a release. Release page titles
Media list names Which media lists exist and their names. News On Demand staff who manage list members, and release editors choosing lists. Media list names
Error log Nothing: it shows the system's recent errors. Nobody. Error log
Website > Project Blue Bridge The public site's mourning switch. The rest of Website is view-only for you. Every visitor to the public site, and every Core administrator by email. Website and Project Blue Bridge

When a new government takes office, you use Government terms and Cabinet change together. When a new government takes office gives the order.

What you see in the side menu

A Core administrator sees every screen under Administration. Under Work you see Website and nothing else, unless your account also holds other roles. To work on releases, subscribers or the Calendar, give your own account the role you need on Users or Calendar access.

Signing in and unsaved changes

The Hub keeps you signed in while its tab is open. Staying signed in, and unsaved changes says what happens when your session ends, and how the Hub asks before you lose changes you haven't saved.

users.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Users decides who can sign in to the Hub and what each person can do there. Only Core administrators see it.

The table lists every staff account with its Name, Email, Sign-in (Password or Microsoft), Roles and Status. A person with Calendar access also shows a line such as "Calendar: Editor (HLTH)"; you change that on Calendar access.

Find someone

  1. Type part of a name or email address in Filter users. You can also type a role as it appears in the table, such as "NRMS Site editor" or "Core Admin", or just a word of it, such as Editor.
  2. The table narrows as you type, and the count shows "Showing 3 of 24 users". Type active or inactive to list people by status.

Add a user

Add the person before they first sign in. Without an account, sign-in tells them "Your account hasn't been set up. Contact an administrator."

  1. Under Add a user, enter their Email. For Microsoft sign-in, use their Microsoft sign-in name, which is usually their government email address.
  2. Enter their Display name.
  3. Under Roles, tick each role they need. Each box shows the role's name, as it appears in the table, and what it allows.
  4. To let them sign in with a password, tick Set a password now and enter a Password (at least 12 characters). Leave it unticked for people who sign in with Microsoft.
  5. Choose Add user. The person appears in the table.

Nobody is emailed. Tell the person their account is ready.

What each role allows

Each role has the same name in the table and beside its box.

Badge What it allows
Core Admin Manage staff users, Project Blue Bridge, and the error log. It also opens every screen under Administration.
NRMS Editor Create, edit, and publish news releases.
NRMS Site editor Edit the public website's carousel, pins, Live Feed, links, and files.
NRMS Viewer View news releases and the website, with no editing.
NoD Viewer Search News on Demand subscribers and see their history, read-only.
NoD Editor Add, edit, deactivate and delete News on Demand subscribers.
NoD Admin Everything a NoD Editor can do, plus News on Demand operations and list categories.
Distribution Send Send media distribution emails.

Calendar roles are not on this screen. Give them on Calendar access.

Change someone's account

  1. Find the person and choose Edit on their row. Their settings open under the row.
  2. Make one change, then choose the button beside it. Each button saves only its own part:
    • To rename them, change the display name and choose Save name. Until you do, "Name not saved yet." shows beside it.
    • To change what they can do, tick or untick roles and choose Save roles. Until you do, "Roles not saved yet." shows beside it. Saving replaces all their roles with the ticked ones.
    • Under Account, each action takes effect on its own: Active, Unlink Microsoft sign-in, and Set password. To set a new password, type it and choose Set password. You see "Password updated." This only appears for people who sign in with a password.
  3. Choose Close on their row when you are done. Anything you typed but did not save stays there until you leave the page.

Deactivate or reactivate someone

  1. Choose Edit on their row.
  2. Switch Active off. The Hub asks "Deactivate {name}?" and explains "They're signed out at once and can't sign in until reactivated."
  3. Choose Deactivate. You see "Saved" beside the switch.

To bring them back, switch Active on. It saves straight away, with no question. They sign in again as usual: reactivating doesn't bring back the session they had.

Link a person who has no email

People brought in from the old Calendar without an email show "No email" and "Inactive until linked to an email." They can't sign in.

  1. Choose Edit on their row.
  2. Enter their address in Email for {name}.
  3. Choose Link and activate. Their email is set and they become active. If they sign in with a password, set one for them as well.

Unlink Microsoft sign-in

After a person's first Microsoft sign-in, their Sign-in shows Microsoft and their password stops working. Unlink them when their Microsoft account was replaced, or when sign-in tells them "Your account needs an administrator to check it."

  1. Choose Edit on their row. It shows "Sign-in: Microsoft (Entra)".
  2. Choose Unlink Microsoft sign-in, then Unlink to confirm.
  3. Ask them to sign in with Microsoft again. Their next Microsoft sign-in links them again by their email address.

Until they do, they are back on password sign-in, and any password they had before works again.

What happens next

  • Deactivating signs the person out at once, everywhere in the Hub. The next thing they do is refused, and the Hub tells them "Your session has ended". If they try to sign in again, they see "Your account is not active. Contact a Core administrator."
  • A role you take away stops working at once: the next thing they try that needs it is refused. Their Hub menus catch up within 10 minutes, or at once if they reload the Hub or come back to its tab.
  • No change on this screen sends an email.

If you leave before saving

If you have changes you haven't saved and you go to another screen or choose your browser's Back, the Hub asks "You have unsaved changes on this page. Leave anyway and discard them?" Choose Stay to keep working, or Leave to discard the changes. Closing or reloading the tab gets your browser's own question. A person's changes count even after you choose Close on their row: the Hub keeps them until you save them or leave.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"a user with that email already exists" Someone already has that address. Filter the table to find them.
"use at least 12 characters" The password is too short.
"you can't remove your own admin access" You tried to take Core Admin off yourself, or to deactivate yourself. Ask another Core administrator.
"this user signs in with Microsoft; unlink them first" Passwords can't be set for Microsoft sign-in. Unlink them first if they really need a password.
"set an email before activating this user" The person has no email. Use Link and activate.
"this user already has an email" The person was linked already. Reload the page.

calendar-access.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Calendar access gives staff a Calendar role and the ministries they work for. Calendar administrators and Calendar system administrators use this screen too, but with limits that don't apply to you.

The table shows each person's Name, Email, Calendar role and Ministries. Inactive people are hidden until you tick Show inactive users, including those with no email.

The Calendar roles

From lowest to highest: Read Only, Editor, Advanced, Administrator, System Administrator. Each person has one role or No Calendar access. What each role can do in the Calendar is in the Calendar manuals.

Members of an HQ organization see every ministry in the Calendar. GCPE Headquarters, GCPE Media Relations and the Office of the Premier are usually HQ. You decide which organizations are HQ on Organizations.

Give or change someone's Calendar access

The person needs a Hub account first. Add them on Users if they have none.

  1. Type part of their name or email in Find a user by name or email.
  2. Choose Edit on their row.
  3. Choose their Calendar role.
  4. Under Ministries, tick every ministry they work for. HQ organizations are marked "— HQ". A role needs at least one ministry.
  5. Choose Save Calendar access. You see "Saved Calendar access for {name}."

Saving replaces the person's whole ministry list with what is ticked.

Remove someone's Calendar access

  1. Choose Edit on their row.
  2. Choose No Calendar access in Calendar role.
  3. Choose Save Calendar access.

What happens next

  • The change reaches the Calendar within a minute.
  • A person whose role was removed sees "You don't have Calendar access" on their next click in the Calendar. They are not signed out of the Hub.
  • Nobody is emailed.

Limits that apply to other administrators

You may change anyone, including yourself. Calendar administrators and Calendar system administrators can't, and the screen shows them a note instead of Edit:

  • "You can't change your own Calendar access."
  • "Only a System Administrator or a Core administrator can change this user's access."
  • "Only an HQ Administrator, a System Administrator or a Core administrator can change this user's access."
  • "Only a Core administrator can give Calendar access to an inactive user who has none."

When one of them sends a request like this to you, make the change yourself.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"choose at least one ministry for a Calendar role" Tick a ministry, or choose No Calendar access.
"Health is no longer active or doesn't exist. Untick it, then save again." The named ministry was deactivated while you were editing. Untick it. A person who already had a deactivated ministry keeps it when you save.

organizations.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Organizations holds every ministry: its name, minister, media contacts and page links, and the settings that decide who sees it. Site editors also open this screen, but they can only edit a ministry's details. Adding, deactivating, handing over and the HQ and Public settings are yours alone.

The table shows each ministry's Name, Abbreviation, Minister, Active, HQ and Public. A ministry that isn't public has a "Not public" badge. Inactive ministries are hidden until you tick Show inactive organizations.

For a new cabinet, prepare all the ministry changes together on Cabinet change instead of one at a time here.

Edit a ministry

  1. Choose Edit on the ministry's row. The form opens above the table.
  2. Change what you need:
    • Ministry name (required) and Additional display name, which shows in brackets under the ministry on the Media Contacts page.
    • Abbreviation and Parent ministry, straight after the names. Only you see these.
    • Sort order: a whole number that places the ministry in lists.
    • Minister name (with the title, such as "Honourable Jane Doe"), Minister summary, Minister email and Minister photo URL. Upload the photo under Website > Files first, choose Copy public address beside it, then paste the address. A preview appears once the address starts with https://. An address copied from the Hub itself shows "This address points at the Hub, which the public can't open. On Website → Files, use Copy public address and paste that instead." Visitors couldn't see that photo.
    • Minister biography: shown on the minister's biography page, linked as Read Bio. Clear the biography removes that page. After you rename the minister, a note warns "The biography still describes the previous minister."
    • Meet the Team links, Media contacts (Primary contact, Alternate contact, After-hours phone) and Ministry page links (Ministry website, Photos (Flickr) address, Videos (YouTube) address, Featured Topics, Featured Services).
    • Active, last, before Save. Only you see it.
  3. Choose Save. You see "Saved. The public ministry pages update within a few minutes."

The public page shows the alternate contact only when there is a primary contact.

The abbreviation

Every release number contains the lead ministry's abbreviation, as in 2026HLTH0001. Use 2 to 10 capital letters or digits. No two active ministries may share one. A release can't be approved until its lead ministry has an abbreviation: release editors see "The lead ministry has no abbreviation yet. Ask an administrator to add one, then approve again." Changing it affects only releases approved from then on.

Add a ministry

  1. Choose Add ministry.
  2. Enter the Ministry name (required). Below it you see the public web address made from the name, such as "Web address: /site/ministries/health/". The web address can't be changed later, even if you rename the ministry.
  3. Enter the Abbreviation if you have it.
  4. Choose Create ministry. The edit form opens so you can fill in the minister and contacts.

Decide who sees a ministry

Tick or untick the boxes on the ministry's row. Each change saves at once and shows "Saved".

  • Public ticked: the ministry is on the public ministry list and the subscribe page. Unticking asks "Remove {ministry} from the public site?" Choose Remove from public site to confirm.
  • HQ ticked: everyone in this organization sees every ministry in the Corporate Calendar and gets its HQ-only fields and actions. Ticking asks "Make {ministry} an HQ organization?" Choose Make HQ to confirm. Unticking takes that view away from every member at once.

Deactivate a ministry, or hand it over to another

Use a hand-over when a ministry is replaced: merged, split or renamed into a new one. A plain rename needs no hand-over: change the name with Edit. The web address, subscribers and history stay.

  1. Choose Deactivate on the ministry's row. A panel titled "Deactivate {ministry}" opens.
  2. In Has a successor?, choose the ministry that takes over its work. For a split, choose Add another successor and pick the next one. Staff, Calendar activities and draft releases go to the first successor.
  3. Under "What moves to {successor}", untick anything that should stay behind. Each box shows how many it moves:
    • "Send {ministry}'s web pages to {successor}" is always on.
    • "Move {n} subscribers to {successors}." Subscribers are added to every successor.
    • "Move {n} staff from {ministry} to {successor}."
    • "Move {n} upcoming Calendar activities and {n} comm contacts to {successor}."
    • "Move {n} draft releases to {successor}." Approved and scheduled releases don't move. They are listed with links so you can change their lead ministry yourself.
    • "Let {successor} use the abbreviation {abbreviation}." This appears when the successor has no abbreviation. If it has one, tick "Replace {successor}'s abbreviation … with …" first.
  4. Choose Deactivate and hand over. You see "{ministry} is deactivated. Its pages now send visitors to {successor}. Moves to other services finish shortly."

While a count loads it says "counting…". "count unavailable" means it couldn't be loaded; you can still go ahead.

To deactivate with nothing moved, leave Has a successor? at No successor and choose Deactivate. The panel warns that the ministry disappears from the public site, its subscribers stop receiving news, and they are not moved anywhere. Unticking Active in the edit form does the same.

Set a successor later

For a ministry that is already inactive, tick Show inactive organizations and choose Set successor… on its row. The panel works the same way. Choose Set successor to finish.

Reactivate a ministry

  1. Tick Show inactive organizations.
  2. Choose Reactivate on its row. You see "{ministry} is active again."

Reactivating stops its pages sending visitors to the successor. It does not move anyone back. It also doesn't change Public: if you see "It isn't public: tick Public to list it on the public site.", tick Public when it should be listed.

What happens next

  • Saved details reach the public Ministries page and each ministry's own page within a few minutes.
  • After a hand-over, the old ministry's public web addresses send visitors to the successor. If the successor is later handed over too, the old addresses go straight to the newest ministry.
  • Subscribers, staff, Calendar activities and drafts move in the background shortly after. If they haven't moved after a few minutes, tell the support team.
  • A deactivated ministry can't be added to anyone's Calendar access. People who already have it keep it.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"No changes to save." Nothing in the form changed.
"That abbreviation is already used by {ministry}." Another active ministry has it. Choose another, or change that ministry's first.
"Use 2 to 10 capital letters or digits, e.g. HLTH." The abbreviation has the wrong form.
"A ministry with this name already exists ({web name})." Use a different name, or edit the existing ministry.
"{ministry} already exists but is inactive. Use Reactivate on its row." Reactivate it instead of adding it again.
"Use at least one letter or number in the name." The name has no letters or digits to make a web address from.
"{third ministry} already uses the abbreviation {abbreviation}. Untick …" During a hand-over, a third ministry holds the old abbreviation. Untick "Let {successor} use the abbreviation" or change that ministry's abbreviation first.
"{ministry} can't be reactivated while {successor} uses its abbreviation …" The successor took the abbreviation. Give one of them a different abbreviation first.
"Choose an active ministry as successor." Pick a successor before choosing Set successor. Inactive ministries can't be successors.
"{successor} already leads back to {ministry}; that would loop." That successor was itself handed over to this ministry. Choose a different successor.

cabinet-change.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Cabinet change lets you prepare every ministry change for a new cabinet, then publish them all together, right away or at the swearing-in time. Open it from the Cabinet change link on Organizations. Nothing changes on the public site or for staff until you publish.

One cabinet change is open at a time. It saves as you go, so you can leave and come back.

Add the changes

To merge ministries, add the new ministry first, then hand each old ministry over to it. To split one, hand it over to more than one successor. To abolish one, hand it over with no successor.

  1. Under Add a change, choose one of:
    • Rename or change a ministry: pick the Ministry, then change its Name, Abbreviation or Minister. Renaming keeps the ministry's web address, subscribers and staff.
    • Add a new ministry: enter its Name, and optionally its Abbreviation (optional) and Minister (optional).
    • Hand over a ministry: pick the Ministry to hand over, then its Successor. A new ministry added in this change can be the successor. Choose "No successor (abolish it)" to close it with nothing moved. The "What moves to …" boxes work as on Organizations.
  2. Choose Add this change. You see "Added:" and a summary. The change is listed under "Changes in this cabinet change".

Remove beside a change takes it out. Removing a new ministry also removes the hand-overs to it, and the page says which.

Preview

  1. Choose Preview. It runs the whole change without saving it.
  2. Read "What will change": each ministry, Now and After publishing. Then "What each hand-over moves" and "Ministries after this change".
  3. If you see "Fix these before publishing", fix each problem listed, then choose Preview again.

When it says "No problems found. You can publish it or schedule it below.", you can publish.

Publish now

  1. Under Publish, choose Publish now…. The page asks "Publish these {n} changes now? This can't be undone in one step."
  2. Choose Yes, publish now, or Not yet to go back.

You see "The cabinet change is published."

Schedule it for the swearing-in

  1. Under Publish, choose Schedule….
  2. Enter the Date and Time (BC time) under "Publish at (BC time)", usually the swearing-in time.
  3. Choose Schedule. The page shows "Publishes on {date} at {time} Pacific."

It publishes by itself; nobody needs to be there. Until then you can still edit it, publish it now, or choose Don't publish at that time (keep it as a draft). Editing a scheduled change takes it off its schedule: preview it and schedule it again.

Start over

Choose Discard this cabinet change…, then Yes, discard it. Nothing is published.

What happens next

  • Publishing makes every change at once: all of it or none of it.
  • The public Ministries page updates within a few minutes.
  • Old ministry pages send visitors to their successors.
  • Subscribers, staff, Calendar activities and draft releases move to their new ministries shortly after.
  • If a scheduled publish can't go through, the change goes back to a draft and the page shows "This change wasn't published" with the reason. Nothing is half done. Fix it, preview again, then publish or schedule it.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Changed by someone else since you added this." Someone edited that ministry after you added the change. Check it on Organizations, then choose Keep this change or Remove.
"{ministries} would both use the abbreviation {abbreviation}." Two active ministries would end up with the same abbreviation. Change one.
"{ministry} is handed over more than once in this change." Remove one of the hand-overs.
"{successor} is handed over in this change, so it can't also take over {ministry}'s work." Hand the ministry straight to the final ministry instead.
"Choose a successor for {ministry}, or choose “No successor (abolish it)”." The hand-over has no successor. Remove it and add it again.
"Nothing was published. Fix the problems listed under Preview, then try again." Preview found problems. Fix them first.
"Enter the date and time to publish." Fill in both fields before Schedule.
"Nothing was scheduled. Choose a time in the future." The time you entered has passed.
"This cabinet change is no longer open. Someone else may have published or discarded it." Reload the page to see what happened.

government-terms.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Government terms sets the dates of each government term. The public archive groups releases by term. You enter only a start date: a term runs until the day before the next one starts, so terms never overlap and no end date is typed.

The table "Government terms, newest first" shows each term's Term, Dates, Status and how many Releases it holds. Status is Current, Past, Scheduled or Undated.

Start a new government term

Do this as soon as the swearing-in date is announced. You can enter it weeks ahead.

  1. Choose Start new government term.
  2. Enter the Start date (required): the first day of the new government, normally the swearing-in date.
  3. Leave Name (optional) empty unless you want one. The public archive always shows the term's dates, with the name beside them if there is one.
  4. Choose Continue. The Hub asks you to confirm, for example "Start a new government term on November 20, 2028? The current term will end November 19, 2028. Releases published from that day are listed under the new term."
  5. Check the dates: the start date decides where every release is listed in the archive.
  6. Choose Confirm, or Go back to change the date.

You see "Saved. The archive switches to the new term on {date}." If the date is today or earlier, you see "Saved. The new term is now the current term."

Fix a term's dates or name

  1. Choose Edit on the term's row.
  2. Change the Name, the Start date, or the Old archive web address. The address is optional and must start with https://.
  3. Choose Save.
  4. If the term has already started and you changed its start date, the Hub asks first, because releases move between terms: "Change the start date to {date}? Releases published from that day will be listed under this term, and the term before it will end the day before." Choose Confirm.

You see "Saved." The archive pages and the current-term link rebuild by themselves.

Delete a scheduled term

Delete appears only on a term that hasn't started and has no releases.

  1. Choose Delete on its row. The Hub asks "Delete the term starting {date}? Nothing is listed under it yet, and the current term stays as it is."
  2. Choose Confirm. You see "The term starting {date} is deleted."

What happens next

  • Each release is listed under the term that covers the day it was published, in BC time. A release published at 11:59 p.m. the day before the start date stays in the old term. One published at 12:00 a.m. on the start date is in the new term.
  • At midnight Pacific on the start date, the public archive gets a page for the new term, and its current-term link points there. This happens even if nothing is published that day.
  • Until the first release, the new term's page says "Nothing has been published in this term yet."
  • An undated term never counts as current and is left out of the public archive. Give it a start date with Edit.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Another term already starts on that date." Choose a different start date.
"Must be after {date} and before {date}." A term's start date can't move past its neighbours. Choose a date between the two shown.
"A term that has started can't be moved to a date after today." Start a new term instead.
"Only a term that hasn't started can be deleted." Started terms stay. Fix their dates with Edit.
"A term with releases can't be deleted." Releases are already listed under it.
"No changes to save." Nothing in the form changed.

sectors-themes-and-tags.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Sectors, themes and tags keeps the three lists that release editors use to file releases. The public site has a page for each one, and subscribers can follow them.

Choose Sectors, Themes or Tags under Show to see one list. Each row has a Key, a Name, an Order and an Active box. The key is part of the public web address and never changes.

Rename, reorder or retire entries

You can change several rows, even across the three lists, and save them together.

  1. Change the Name or Order on any row. Order is a whole number; lower numbers come first.
  2. To retire an entry, untick Active. To bring one back, tick it again.
  3. Changed rows show "Unsaved", and a note below the table counts them, such as "2 rows have unsaved changes".
  4. Choose Save changes. If you retired anything, the Hub asks "Retire {name}?" and explains that it leaves the public site's lists, the subscribe page and the release editor's choices. Choose Retire.

You see "Saved {n} changes."

Add a sector, theme or tag

  1. Choose the list under Show.
  2. Under Add a sector (or theme, or tag), enter the Name. The Key fills in from the name; you can change it. Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.
  3. Choose Add sector (or Add theme, Add tag). You see "Added {name} ({key})."

The new entry goes to the end of the list and is active. Adding never changes an entry that already exists. If the key is taken, you see a message beside the form and nothing is added.

What happens next

  • Changes reach the public site, the subscribe page and the release editor within a minute.
  • A retired entry leaves those lists. Releases already filed under it keep it.
  • Nobody is emailed.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Name is required." Enter a name.
"Name is too long (at most 100 characters)." Shorten the name.
"Order must be a whole number." Enter a number such as 3.
"Keys use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens (at most 100)." Fix the key.
"A sector with the key health already exists: Health." (or "A theme…", "A tag…") The key is taken, and the message names the entry that has it. Choose another key. To bring a retired entry back, tick Active on its row.
"{n} rows couldn't be saved — see the message on those rows." The other rows were saved. Fix the rows with a message and save again.
"No changes to save." Nothing was changed.

release-page-titles.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Release page titles lists the titles a new release can choose, such as News Release or Information Bulletin. The title shows above the headline on the public release page.

Titles are grouped by release type: Release, Story, Factsheet, Update and Advisory. Each row has a Page title, Language (English or French), Order, Layout (Formal or Informal) and Page image.

Change a page title

  1. Change the fields on the row.
  2. Choose Save on that row. You see "Saved {title}."

Add a page title

  1. Under Add a page title, choose the Type.
  2. Enter the Page title: up to 50 characters, without < or >.
  3. Choose the Language. Release editors choosing a title on New release see the English titles.
  4. Leave Order as suggested, or change it. Lower numbers come first.
  5. Choose the Layout and Page image that a new release with this title starts with. A Formal document has an organizations line; an Informal document has a byline.
  6. Choose Add page title. You see "Added {title}."

Delete a page title

  1. Choose Delete on its row. The Hub asks "Delete {title}?" and explains "New releases can no longer choose it. Releases that already use it keep it."
  2. Choose Delete.

What happens next

  • Release editors see the change the next time they open New release.
  • A release keeps the title it was given. To change a published release's title, edit that release.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Page title is required." Enter a title.
"Page title can't contain < or >." Remove those characters.
"Order must be a whole number from 0 to 9999." Fix the order.
"A page title with that name already exists in that language." Choose another title, or edit the existing one.
"This is the only English page title for {type}. Add another first." Each release type needs at least one English title. Add the new one, then delete the old one.
"That page image does not exist." The image was removed. Choose another one.
"That page title no longer exists." Someone else deleted or renamed it. The list reloads.

media-list-names.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Media list names decides which media lists exist, what they are called and the order they appear in. Release editors pick these lists to send a release to reporters. The reporters on each list are managed by News On Demand staff under Subscribers > Media lists. If you also have a News on Demand role, the screen's "Subscribers, Media lists" is a link there.

Each row has a Key, a Name, an Order and an Active box.

Rename or reorder a list

  1. Change the Name or Order on its row.
  2. Choose Save on that row. You see "{key} saved."

Retire a list

  1. Untick Active on its row.
  2. Choose Save. The Hub asks "Retire {key}?" and explains "Releases can no longer be sent to it. Its members are kept, and ticking Active again brings it back."
  3. Choose Retire list.

Add a list

  1. Under Add a media list, enter the Key: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. It can't be changed later.
  2. Enter the Name.
  3. Choose Add media list. You see "Media list added. It reaches News On Demand within a minute."

What happens next

  • Changes reach News On Demand's media lists within a minute.
  • A retired list can't be put on a release. A release that already had it shows it ticked, greyed out and marked "(retired)"; nothing is sent to it.
  • Nobody is emailed.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"A media list with that key already exists." Choose another key. To bring back a retired list, tick Active on its row.
"Keys use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; both fields are required." Fix the key, and fill in both fields.
"Name is required." Enter a name.
"Order must be a whole number." Enter a number such as 3.

error-log.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Error log shows the most recent errors the system recorded, newest first, so you can tell the support team what went wrong and when. It changes nothing.

Check for errors

  1. Open Error log. It shows up to 200 errors, the most recent first, or "No errors logged."
  2. Choose Refresh to load newer entries.
  3. Each row shows When it last happened, How often, a Process ID and the Message.

An error that happened more than once, with exactly the same message, is shown once. How often says "Once", or how many times and when it first happened, such as "212 times, first Oct 4, 2026 10:00 AM". So one problem that repeats every few minutes doesn't push the other errors out of view.

When you report a problem, copy the time and the whole message. The Process ID tells the support team which run of the system logged the last one.

What to know

  • Entries are kept when the system restarts.
  • Values quoted in errors about stored records, such as an email address, are blanked out before the entry is kept.
  • If the page says "Couldn't load the error log.", reload it. If that keeps happening, the system itself may be down: tell the support team.
  • An update that one part of the system couldn't deliver to another for 24 hours is logged here once, and listed on Undelivered updates, where you can send it again.

undelivered-updates.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

Undelivered updates lists the updates one part of the system sent to another that weren't accepted within 24 hours. For example, a published release that never reached Subscribers (News On Demand), so no one was emailed, or a ministry change that never reached Releases. The system keeps trying each update for 24 hours before it lists it here.

"Nothing is waiting: every update was delivered." means all is well.

What the table shows

The newest are first.

Column What it shows
When When the update was sent.
From The part of the system that sent it, such as Releases, Core administration, Email sending, News service or Calendar.
Update What it was about, such as "Release published: Highway 11 traffic change" or "Organization deactivated: health".
Not accepted by The part of the system that refused it, such as Subscribers (News On Demand) or Public site.
Last error The last reason it failed, such as HTTP 503, shortened if it is long.

The table never shows an update's full text. A Calendar activity shows only its number, such as "Activity 12".

If one part has more than 200 waiting, a line above the table says so, and only the 200 most recent from it are listed.

Replaced updates

A row that says "Replaced by a newer update: not sent again" has no Retry. A later update about the same record, to the same part of the system, takes its place. For example, a release was published and then unpublished while Subscribers (News On Demand) was refusing both. The unpublish is what counts now, so the system never sends the older one again: it would email subscribers about a release that was withdrawn. Send the newer one, or dismiss both. Replaced updates don't count in the health check.

Only an update that carries everything the older one did replaces it. A release's correction doesn't replace its publish: subscribers only hear about a release from the publish.

Overtaken updates

A row that says "A later change got there first, so it can't be sent again" has no Retry either. A later update about the same record already reached that part of the system, but it can't stand in for this one. For example, a release was published while Subscribers (News On Demand) was refusing it, and a correction reached it later. Subscribers never got the release, and sending the publish now would be ignored. These keep counting in the health check until you deal with them:

  • For a release, publish it again from Releases, then dismiss the row here.
  • For anything else, make the change again where it was made, then dismiss the row.

Send one again

Before you retry, check that the part named under Not accepted by is working, or ask your operations team. The Error log usually shows why it refused.

  1. Choose Retry on its row. The button shows "Retrying…" until the system answers.
  2. You see "Queued for delivery again." and the row leaves the table. The system tries once more within the next minute.

If it fails again, it comes straight back to the table, without another 24 hours of tries. Choose Refresh after a minute to check.

Retrying sends the update as it was, now. A "Release published" update then emails that release's subscribers, however late. Check the release is still published, and still worth emailing, before you retry it.

Send them all again

When one part has more than one waiting, a button such as Retry all 3 from Releases appears above the table. It asks first: how many it will send again, how many replaced or overtaken updates it leaves out, and, for Releases, that published releases email their subscribers. Choose Resend to send them, oldest first, or Cancel.

Dismiss an update

An update that doesn't need sending any more can be dismissed: for example because the change was made again by hand, or the receiving part was retired. A dismissed update is never sent.

  • Choose Dismiss on its row. You see "Dismissed: it won't be sent." and the row leaves the table.
  • Dismiss all, above the table, dismisses every undelivered update, from every part, including any not listed. It asks first.

The Dismissed table below lists the most recent dismissals, with when and who dismissed each.

What is safe

  • Retrying an update that was in fact received is harmless: the receiving part ignores a copy it already has.
  • The system never resends a replaced or overtaken update, on its own or with Retry all.
  • What retrying can't undo is an email. A retried "Release published" emails subscribers when it is sent.

What to know

  • The Calendar's system administrators also see the Calendar's own updates on Calendar > Undelivered events. Retrying from either screen does the same thing.
  • The system's health check, which the operations team monitors, reports "degraded" while any update from the last 7 days is waiting here. Replaced and dismissed updates don't count; overtaken ones do. Retrying or dismissing is what clears it.

website-project-blue-bridge.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin).

In Website, the one thing only you can change is Project Blue Bridge: the switch that puts the public site into mourning when the King dies. Everything else in Website is view-only for you.

What you can and can't change in Website

You can open every Website tab: Carousel, Emergency pins, Live Feed, What's featured where, Resource links, Files, Website log and Site settings. You see what is live, but there are no Save or Publish buttons.

Site editors make those changes. The Site editor manual explains what each tab does. If your work needs them, give your own account the NRMS Site editor role on Users.

Website log lists every change to the public site's content: who, when and what. Use it to check who changed something.

Turn Project Blue Bridge on or off

Turn it on only with approval from the Intergovernmental Relations Secretariat (IGRS). The same steps turn it off.

  1. Open Website > Site settings > Project Blue Bridge. The page shows "Project Blue Bridge is currently OFF." (or ON).
  2. Choose the Project Blue Bridge switch. A box asks "Turn Project Blue Bridge on?" and repeats the warning "Do not click OK unless you have approval from IGRS".
  3. Type KING CHARLES III in Type KING CHARLES III to confirm, in capitals, exactly.
  4. Tick IGRS has approved this change.
  5. Choose Confirm turn on (or Confirm turn off). Until steps 3 and 4 are done, the button stays greyed out.

The page then shows "Project Blue Bridge is currently ON."

The banner's wording is on Site settings > Site identity, which site editors change.

What happens next

  • The public site changes to its mourning theme, with a black banner announcing the King's death. The home page changes within a few minutes; older pages follow over the following minutes, newest first.
  • Every active Core administrator gets an email such as "Project Blue Bridge turned ON on {site}", saying who changed it and when.
  • The change is listed in Website log.
  • Turning it off puts the site back the same way.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Someone else changed this — reload to see their changes." Someone else changed the switch while you had the page open. Choose Reload and check its state.

site-editor-overview.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

You run what the public news site shows around the news releases: the home page carousel, emergency notices, links, files, the banner, the footer, colours and wording. You also keep each ministry's minister and contact details up to date.

What only you can do

Release editors and release viewers can open Website, but they see only What's featured where and Website log. Core administrators see every Website tab but can't change anything except Project Blue Bridge. Everything below is yours.

Screen What it controls When visitors see it Help page
Website > Carousel The slides at the top of the home page, and the next set of slides with its go-live time. A few minutes after you publish, or after the next set's go-live time. Carousel
Website > Emergency pins Two emergency notices you can pin to the home page. A few minutes after you save a pinned notice, or pin it. Emergency pins
Website > Live Feed The Live Webcast button and the stream it plays. A few minutes after you save. Live Feed
Website > Resource links The list of links on the home page. A few minutes after you save. Resource links
Website > Files Files the public can open at a fixed web address, such as PDFs and minister photos. As soon as the upload finishes. Files
Website > Site settings The banner, footer, social links, colours, headings, page wording, menu and site description. A few minutes after you publish. How site settings are published
Organizations Each ministry's name, minister, biography, media contacts and page links. Within a few minutes of saving. Organizations

What's featured where and Website log are read-only for everyone. See What's featured where and the Website log.

What you see in the side menu

Under Work you see Releases, Search and Website. Under Administration you see Organizations.

On Releases and Search you can read releases but not change them. Choosing a release's Top or Feature spot is done on the release itself, by release editors. To write or publish releases, ask a Core administrator for the release editor role as well. The Releases editor manual and the Releases viewer manual cover release work.

carousel.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

The carousel is the set of slides at the top of the public home page. Visitors see one slide at a time and move between them with Previous and Next; the slides don't turn by themselves.

Carousel has three parts:

  • Live: the slides visitors see now.
  • Next: a copy you can prepare ahead, with a time when it replaces the live slides. There is at most one.
  • Past: the last five sets that were replaced, for reference. You can't change them.

Each slide has a Headline, Summary, Action URL (where the slide's link goes), Action label (the link's words), Facebook post URL, Justify (Left or Right) and an image.

Change the live slides

Changes to the live slides go to the public home page when you publish them.

  1. Change what you need in a slide's fields.
  2. To move a slide, choose Move up or Move down on it, or drag it by its handle.
  3. To remove a slide, choose Remove on it, then Confirm remove. It leaves the live slides when you publish.
  4. To add a slide, choose Add slide and fill in its fields.
  5. Choose Publish carousel changes. A box asks "Publish these carousel changes now?"
  6. Choose Publish carousel changes again to confirm. Under the live slides you see "Published at 2:30 PM. Live now: the public home page shows the changes within a few minutes." (with the time).

If next slides are waiting to go live, the box also says "The next carousel was copied from these slides on {date and time}, so it won't include these changes. When it goes live on {date and time}, it replaces them. Make the same changes on the next carousel too." The next slides are a copy made when you created them, and they replace the live slides whole. So a fix you publish now, such as a corrected link, is undone at the go-live time unless you make it on the next slides as well.

Leave Action label empty to use the standard link words, set on Navigation and labels.

To link to a file from Files, paste the address from its Copy public address button. An address copied from the Hub itself shows "This address points at the Hub, which the public can't open. On Website → Files, use Copy public address and paste that instead."

Add or change a slide's image

Use a JPEG or PNG image of up to 2 MB. Any slide can take an image, including one you have just added.

  1. Choose the slide's Image (JPEG or PNG, up to 2 MB) button and pick the file.
  2. What happens next depends on the slide:
    • On the live slides, the slide says "New image chosen:" and the file's name. The image goes live with your other changes when you choose Publish carousel changes and confirm. Until then the slide keeps the image it had. Website log notes that you chose it.
    • On a slide you have just added to the next slides, the image is saved when you choose Save carousel.
    • On a slide already saved in the next slides, the image saves as soon as you choose it, and you see "Slide 2 image saved at 2:30 PM. Not live yet." Nothing changes on the public site.

The slide shows the new image as soon as it is saved or published.

Prepare the next slides

  1. Under Next, enter the Date and Time (BC time) in Go live at (BC time).
  2. Choose Create next carousel. It starts as a copy of the live slides, images included. Next then says "Copied from the live carousel on {date and time}. It goes live on {date and time}."
  3. Change, add, remove and reorder slides as above.
  4. Choose Save carousel. Nothing changes on the public site. You see "Saved at 2:30 PM. Not live yet: this carousel goes live on {date and time}."

If someone publishes changes to the live slides after the copy was made, Next warns "The live carousel was changed on {date and time}, after this copy was made. Those changes aren't in this carousel: make them here too, or they'll be undone when it goes live." Compare the two sets and make the same changes on the next slides.

At the go-live time, the next slides replace the live ones by themselves, and the old live slides move to Past. To change the time, enter a new one in Go live at (BC time) and choose Save carousel.

To switch now instead, choose Make live now, then Confirm make live. You see "The next carousel went live at 2:30 PM. Live now: the public home page shows it within a few minutes."

To throw the next slides away, choose Delete next carousel, then Confirm delete. This can't be undone.

What happens next

  • The public home page shows published changes within a few minutes.
  • Every change is listed in Website log under Carousel, with your name.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Slide 2: Enter a full web address for Action URL, starting with http:// or https://" The web address in Action URL (or Facebook post URL) on that slide is wrong. Start it with http:// or https://, or empty the box. Nothing is saved until every address is right.
"Keep the action label to 40 characters or fewer, in plain text." Shorten the Action label, and remove any < or > characters.
"Choose a go-live time in the future." The go-live time has already passed.
"Upload a JPEG or PNG image." The file isn't a JPEG or PNG image.
"That image is over 2 MB. Choose a smaller image." Make the image smaller and try again.
"Choose slide 2’s image again." The image you chose for that slide wasn't kept. Pick the file again, then publish or save.
"Someone else changed this — reload to see their changes." Another site editor saved these slides while you had the page open. Choose Reload. Your unsaved changes are lost, so make them again.

emergency-pins.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

Emergency pins holds two emergency notices, Primary and Secondary. A pinned notice shows on the public home page under the Emergency information heading, above the news. An unpinned one is kept here but not shown.

Each notice has the same fields as a carousel slide: headline, summary, action URL, action label, Facebook post URL, justify and an image.

Write a notice

  1. Fill in the notice's fields, such as Primary headline and Primary summary.
  2. Choose Save primary pin (or Save secondary pin).

If the notice is already pinned, the change goes to the public site when you save. Under the notice you see "Saved at 2:30 PM. Live now: the home page shows it within a few minutes." (with the time). An unpinned notice says "Saved at 2:30 PM. Not on the home page: this notice isn't pinned."

To link to a file from Files, paste the address from its Copy public address button into the action URL. An address copied from the Hub itself shows "This address points at the Hub, which the public can't open. On Website → Files, use Copy public address and paste that instead."

Pin or unpin a notice

Save the notice first. If you have typed changes you haven't saved, the switch does nothing and shows "Save your changes first." Your typing stays.

  1. Choose the switch beside Primary is not pinned, below Save primary pin. It saves at once, with no question, and changes only the pin; it now reads Primary is pinned, and you see "Pinned at 2:30 PM. Live now: the home page shows this notice within a few minutes."
  2. To take the notice down, choose the switch again. You see "Unpinned at 2:30 PM. The home page stops showing this notice within a few minutes."

Add or change the image

  1. Choose Primary image (JPEG or PNG, up to 2 MB) and pick the file.
  2. It saves at once, and the new image shows above the button straight away. You see "Image saved at 2:30 PM." On a pinned notice the public site changes too, and the message adds "Live now: the home page shows it within a few minutes."

What happens next

  • The public home page shows the change within a few minutes.
  • Every save, pin and unpin is listed in Website log under Emergency pins.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Add a headline before pinning." The saved notice has no headline. Enter one, choose Save primary pin, then pin it.
"Primary: Enter a full web address for Action URL, starting with http:// or https://" The web address in the action URL (or Facebook post URL) is wrong. Start it with http:// or https://, or empty the box. Nothing is saved until it is right.
"Keep the action label to 40 characters or fewer, in plain text." Shorten the action label, and remove any < or > characters.
"Upload a JPEG or PNG image." The file isn't a JPEG or PNG image.
"That image is over 2 MB. Choose a smaller image." Make the image smaller and try again.
"Save your changes first." You changed the notice and then used the pin switch. Choose Save primary pin (or Save secondary pin), then use the switch.
"Someone else changed this — reload to see their changes." Another site editor changed this notice while you had the page open. Choose Reload.

live-feed.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

Live Feed controls the public site's Live Webcast button, which plays a live stream such as a news conference.

  • M3U URL is the address of the stream itself. It is needed to turn the feed on.
  • Manifest URL is optional. The public site doesn't use it.

Both addresses come from whoever runs the webcast. Choose ? beside a field for a short explanation.

Turn the Live Feed on

  1. Enter the M3U URL, and the Manifest URL if you have one.
  2. Switch Live Feed on on.
  3. Choose Save Live Feed. You see "Saved at 2:30 PM. Live now: the Live Webcast button shows on the public site within a few minutes." (with the time).

The Live Webcast button shows on every page while Live Feed on is switched on. Pages that are already open pick up the change within a minute. Turn the feed off when the webcast ends.

The wording around the webcast, such as the button's label and the text shown when nothing is live, is on Navigation and labels and Page text.

Turn the Live Feed off

  1. Switch Live Feed on off.
  2. Choose Save Live Feed. You see "Saved at 2:30 PM. The Live Feed is off: the Live Webcast button goes from the public site within a few minutes."

What happens next

  • The button shows or goes within a few minutes.
  • Website log lists "Turned the Live Feed on", "Turned the Live Feed off" or "Changed the Live Feed URLs", with your name.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Add the M3U playlist URL before turning the Live Feed on." Enter the M3U URL first.
"Live Feed URLs must be https:// or empty." Both addresses must start with https://.
"Someone else changed this — reload to see their changes." Another site editor saved the Live Feed while you had the page open. Choose Reload.

resource-links.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

Resource links is the list of links shown on the public home page under the Resources heading, in the order you set.

Change the links

  1. To change a link, edit its Link 1 text or Link 1 URL (and so on for each link).
  2. To add one, choose Add link and fill in the new boxes at the end.
  3. To move one, choose Move link 1 up or Move link 1 down, or drag it by its handle.
  4. To remove one, choose Remove link 1. It goes at once, with no question, but nothing is saved yet.
  5. Choose Save links. This saves the whole list as it stands. You see "Saved at 2:30 PM. Live now: the public home page shows the resource links within a few minutes." (with the time).

A link's address must start with http:// or https://, or with / for a page on the public site, such as /files/media-guide.pdf. For a file, you can also paste the address from its Copy public address button on Files. An address copied from the Hub itself shows "This address points at the Hub, which the public can't open. On Website → Files, use Copy public address and paste that instead."

If you change your mind before saving, reload the page. The list goes back to what is saved.

What happens next

  • The home page shows the new list within a few minutes.
  • Website log lists "Saved 3 resource links" (with the number), with your name.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"{link text}" needs an http(s) URL or one starting with "/". That link's address is missing or has the wrong form.
"{link text}" needs text of 255 characters or fewer. Shorten the link's words.
"Someone else changed this — reload to see their changes." Another site editor saved the list while you had the page open. Choose Reload. Your unsaved changes are lost.

website-files.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

Files holds documents and images the public can open at a fixed web address, such as a media guide or a minister's photo. You can upload any type of file of up to 512 MB.

The list shows the 50 newest files, each linked to its public address. To find an older one, type part of its name in Search files and choose Search.

Upload a file

  1. Choose Upload a file (any type, up to 512 MB) and pick the file.
  2. The file appears at the top of the list when the upload finishes.

The file's public name is made from your file name: in lower case, with spaces and any character other than letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores turned into hyphens. For example, "Media Guide 2026.PDF" becomes media-guide-2026.pdf. Its public address ends in /files/ and that name, as in /files/media-guide-2026.pdf.

PDFs, images, Office documents, audio, video and text open in the visitor's browser. Anything else, such as a web page, an SVG drawing or a program, is downloaded, never shown on the site.

To use a file elsewhere, such as a minister's photo on Organizations or a link on Resource links, open it from the list and copy the full address from your browser's address bar.

Replace a file

Replacing keeps the file's name and address, so every link to it keeps working.

  1. Upload a file with the same name. A box says "A file named "{name}" already exists".
  2. Choose Replace it. To keep the old file instead, choose Cancel and rename your file.

Visitors may see the old copy for up to a minute.

Delete a file

  1. Choose Delete {name} beside the file.
  2. A box asks "Delete {name}?" and warns "This deletes the file from the public site. It can't be undone."
  3. Choose Confirm delete.

Links to a deleted file stop working. Check that nothing still points to it first.

This includes files brought over from the old news.gov site: once you delete one, its address no longer opens the old site's copy either, in any mix of capital and small letters. Uploading the file again gives it the public name described under Upload a file. If that is the same name, the address works again.

What happens next

  • Website log lists each upload, replacement and deletion under Files, with the file's name and yours.
  • Nobody is emailed.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"{name}: A file can be at most 512 MB." The file is too big to upload.
"The file is empty." The file has nothing in it. Check you picked the right one.
"{name}" is a reserved Windows device name; rename the file. Names such as con, aux, nul or prn can't be used. Rename the file and upload it again.
"The upload wasn't accepted. Reload the page and try again." Most often this happens just after the Hub was updated: a page left open from before the update sends the file in a way the Hub no longer accepts.

site-settings.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

Website > Site settings lists the screens that set how the public site looks and reads: Site banner, Footer links, Social links, Theme colours, Ministry page headings, Media contacts page, Page text, Navigation and labels and Site identity. They all save and publish the same way. Settings history lists everything published so far.

Your draft

You have one private draft that covers all of these screens. Other site editors have their own, and nobody else sees yours.

  • Save draft keeps your changes in your draft. The public site doesn't change.
  • Publish puts your draft live: the changes on this screen, and any you saved as a draft on other settings screens. It asks first, and can publish only this screen instead (see below).
  • Discard draft throws your whole draft away, on every settings screen. A box asks "Discard your whole draft?" and names the other screens it clears, such as "This also throws away your draft changes on Theme colours and Footer links." If you have typed something on this screen and not saved it, the box says that goes too. Choose Discard draft to confirm, or Cancel. The screen then shows what is live: "Draft discarded. Showing what is live."

The foot of each screen says where you are. "Draft saved · not yet live" means you have a draft; "No unpublished changes" means you don't. With a draft, "Your draft has changes on:" names each screen it changes, with a link to it. The next line shows the live revision, who published it and when. Above the buttons, "Publish and Discard draft apply to your whole draft, on every settings screen. Publish lets you publish only this screen instead."

Publish a change

  1. Make the change on the settings screen.
  2. If you like, type a Note for the history log (optional), such as "Election notice". It shows in Settings history and Website log.
  3. Choose Publish. A box asks "Publish your changes?" and lists the screens whose changes go live, such as "Compared with what is live now, this publishes changes on: Site banner and Footer links." Anything you have typed on this screen counts, even if you haven't saved it.
  4. Choose Publish to confirm, or Cancel. You see "Published revision 5. Visitors see it within a few minutes." (with the new number).

Publish only this screen

When your draft also has changes on other settings screens, the box offers two buttons instead of Publish:

  • Publish only Site banner (the button names the screen you are on): only this screen's changes go live. Your changes on the other screens stay in your draft, unpublished. You see "Published revision 6, with only your Site banner changes. Visitors see it within a few minutes. Your draft still has changes on Footer links." In Settings history and Website log, the revision's note starts "Banner only", so it is clear that only that part was published.
  • Publish all changes: your whole draft goes live, as before.

Use Publish only when something is urgent, such as an emergency banner, and you haven't finished or checked the other screens. It works even if someone else has published other screens since you started your draft: what they published stays live, and your draft keeps your other changes. You can use Publish only on the same screen again, for example to fix a typo. It stops only if someone else has changed this same screen since you started (see "If someone else published first"). If another screen in your draft has a problem, the box says so, such as "Footer links has problems that block publishing all changes. Publish only Site banner still works."

If the changes being published have a problem, nothing is published. You see "Draft saved, but it has problems to fix before it can be published." Each problem shows under its field. A problem on another settings screen shows in a list headed "Other parts of the draft have problems that block publishing:", led by a link to that screen. Fix it there, or choose Discard draft to start again from what is live.

Links to files

To link to a file from Files, such as a PDF in the footer, a banner link or the Connect page's Policy link URL, paste the address from its Copy public address button. An address copied from the Hub itself shows "This address points at the Hub, which the public can't open. On Website → Files, use Copy public address and paste that instead." under its Web address: visitors couldn't open it.

If someone else published first

When another site editor publishes while you are working, your Publish doesn't go through. You see "Someone published while you were editing", with who published and when, and "Nothing of yours was published, and your draft is saved." It also lists the screens where your draft differs.

Choose one:

  • Keep my site banner, on top of their version (the button names the screen you are on, such as "Keep my footer links"): your changes on this screen are added to what they published. Changes you saved on other screens stay in your draft too. If they changed one of those screens as well, the message names it, such as "Your draft still has your changes on Footer links, which they changed too: check them before you publish them." Check the result, then choose Publish.
  • Discard mine, use theirs: your draft is thrown away and the screen shows what is live.

Bring back an earlier version

Settings history lists every published revision, newest first, with Revision, When, Who and Note. The live one is marked Live.

  1. Choose Restore… on the revision you want.
  2. A box asks "Restore revision 1?" and lists the screens it would change, such as "Compared with what is live now, this changes: Footer links." If the banner changes, it says what the banner would be.
  3. Choose Restore revision 1. You see "Revision 1 is live again, as revision 6."

Nothing is ever deleted. A restore is published as a new revision, so you can undo it by restoring the one before. Restoring also throws away your own draft.

What happens next

  • Visitors see a published change within a few minutes. Colours and the banner show quickest. A footer change reaches every page over the following minutes.
  • Website log lists each publish under Site settings, such as "Published revision 5: Election notice".
  • Nobody is emailed.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Nothing was restored: revision {n} was published while you were looking. Check it and try again." Someone published while the restore box was open. The list is now up to date.
"Revision {n} can't be restored: it doesn't pass the checks the site settings must meet now." The old revision breaks a rule added since. Make the change by hand instead.
"Revision {n} no longer exists." Reload the page.
"Couldn't load the site settings." Reload the page. If it keeps happening, tell the support team.

site-banner.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

The banner is a notice across the top of every public page, such as planned maintenance or an emergency. Open it from Website > Site settings > Site banner. Like every site setting, it changes the public site only when you publish. See How site settings are published.

Put up a banner

  1. Under Banner type, choose Information or Emergency. Emergency uses the emergency banner colour, set on Theme colours.
  2. Type the Message: plain text, up to 300 characters. The count shows below the box.
  3. To add a link, choose + Add a link, then fill in Link text and Web address. Add more the same way. Remove link 1 takes one away.
  4. To show it later, enter Show from. To take it down by itself, enter Hide after. Both are BC time. Leave Show from blank to show it at once, and Hide after blank to keep it up until you turn it off.
  5. Tick Visitors can close the banner to give it a close button (×).
  6. Check the Preview. It shows roughly how the banner looks.
  7. Choose Publish.

The banner switches on and off by itself at the Show from and Hide after times. You don't need to publish again at those times.

Take the banner down

  1. Under Banner type, choose Off. The preview says "The banner is off, so visitors don't see it." The message and links are kept for next time.
  2. Choose Publish.

What visitors see

  • The banner shows within a few minutes of publishing.
  • It needs JavaScript in the visitor's browser.
  • While Project Blue Bridge is on, its own black banner shows instead, and yours is hidden.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Enter a message, or turn the banner off." Banner type is Information or Emergency, but Message is empty.
"Keep the message to 300 characters or fewer." Shorten the message.
"Use plain text. Add links below instead of HTML." The message has < or > in it. Put links in the link boxes.
"The end time must be after the start time." Hide after is not later than Show from.
"Enter the link text." A link has a web address but no words.
"Must start with https:// or / (a page on this site)." A link's web address is missing, starts with http://, or has a space in it.

theme-colours.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

Theme colours sets the public site's colours: Header and buttons, Text on the header and buttons, Accent, Body text, Secondary text, Panels, Page background, Borders, Information banner, Emergency banner and Section bar colour (Connect page). Open it from Website > Site settings > Theme.

Change a colour

  1. Type the colour's code, such as #013366, in its box. Or choose the colour square beside it and pick a colour.
  2. Check the badge beside the colour. "Readable 7.7:1" means text on it is easy to read. "Too faint 2.3:1" means it isn't.
  3. Check the Preview. It shows the colours you are editing, not the live ones.
  4. Choose Publish. See How site settings are published.

A colour that is too faint can be saved in your draft, but it can't be published. Pick a darker shade until every badge says Readable.

Reset to defaults puts the standard colours back in the boxes. You see "Colours reset to the defaults. Save or publish to keep them." Nothing changes on the site until you publish.

What visitors see

New colours show within a few minutes of publishing.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Use a colour like #013366." The code must be # and six letters or digits.
"Too faint to read behind white text (2.3:1, needs 4.5:1). Pick a darker shade." Text on or in this colour would be hard to read. The message says where: on the page background, on panels, on the header, as link text or behind white text.

footer-and-navigation.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

Two settings screens set the wording around every public page: Footer for the footer's links, and Navigation and labels for the menu, buttons and headings. Open them from Website > Site settings. Both change the public site only when you publish. See How site settings are published.

Footer

The screen is titled Footer links.

  • Help text: a short line in the footer, plain text, up to 200 characters.
  • Help links, Connect with Us links and More Info links: the footer's link lists.
  • Copyright holder: shown as "© 2026 Government of British Columbia", with the current year added for you.
  • Land acknowledgement: shown in a band above the footer on every page. Leave it empty to hide the band.

To change a list:

  1. Choose + Add a link under the list, then fill in Link text and Web address.
  2. Use Move link 1 up, Move link 1 down and Remove link 1 to arrange it.
  3. Choose Publish.

A footer column shows only when it has links. Its heading is on Navigation and labels.

A footer change reaches every page over the following minutes, not all at once.

Navigation and labels

Every wording box is required, except the two footer headings.

  • Header: News menu label, Live webcast button label, up to 4 Header links after the news menu, and Show the search box in the header.
  • Footer headings: Footer: Connect with Us column heading and Footer: More Info column heading. Leave one blank for no heading.
  • Page labels: headings and link words on the home page and news lists, such as Resources heading, Emergency information heading and Load more news button label. The hint under each box says where it appears. Two are never shown on screen; screen readers read them aloud: Slideshow name (read aloud by screen readers) and Home page main heading (hidden, for screen readers).
  • Slide link label (when a slide has none): the link words for a carousel slide or emergency notice whose own Action label is empty.
  • Listing titles: the titles of the releases, stories, factsheets and updates pages.

Change the wording, then choose Publish.

The site's name and logo in the header are not set here. The support team sets them.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Enter text for this field." A required box is empty.
"Keep it to 60 characters or fewer." Shorten the wording. The limit depends on the box.
"Use plain text." Remove < and > from the wording.
"Keep the list to 4 or fewer." There are more than 4 header links.
"Enter the link text." A link has a web address but no words.
"Must start with https:// or / (a page on this site)." A link's web address is missing, starts with http://, or has a space in it.
"Enter who holds the copyright." Copyright holder is empty.
"Keep the help text to 200 characters or fewer." Shorten Help text.
"Keep the land acknowledgement to 1000 characters or fewer." Shorten Land acknowledgement.

ministry-pages-and-media-contacts.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

Two settings screens set the wording that every ministry shares. A single ministry's own details, such as its minister and contacts, are on Organizations. Both screens change the public site only when you publish. See How site settings are published.

Ministry page headings

Website > Site settings > Ministry pages sets the seven headings on every ministry's public page: More from this Ministry heading, Ministry website heading, Ministry photos heading, Ministry videos heading, Featured topics heading, Featured services heading and Media contacts heading.

  1. Change the heading.
  2. Choose Publish.

Each heading is required: plain text, up to 60 characters. Reset to defaults puts the standard headings back in the boxes. You see "Headings reset to the defaults. Save or publish to keep them."

The ministry pages change within a few minutes.

Media contacts page

Website > Site settings > Media contacts page sets the public page that lists media contacts.

  • Page heading (required), Contact line heading and List heading.
  • Introduction: formatted text with bold, italic, lists and links. Include the 24-hour media line number here.
  • Other media contacts: contacts that aren't a ministry's, such as a central media line. Each ministry's own contacts come from its Organizations form.

To add another contact:

  1. Choose Add contact.
  2. Fill in Group and Name (both required), and if you like Group link, Subgroup, Phone, Cell and Email.
  3. Under Placement, choose Above the ministries or Below the ministries.
  4. Use Move contact 1 up, Move contact 1 down or Remove contact 1 to arrange the list. You can have up to 30.
  5. Choose Publish.

A contact row left completely blank is dropped when you save.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Enter a heading." A ministry page heading is empty.
"Use plain text, 60 characters or fewer." Shorten the ministry page heading, and remove any < or > characters.
"Enter text for this field." A required box, such as Page heading, Group or Name, is empty.
"Enter an email address like name@gov.bc.ca." Fix the contact's Email.
"Must start with https:// or / (a page on this site)." Fix the contact's Group link.
"Keep the list to 30 or fewer." Remove a contact.

site-editor-organizations.html:
Who this is for: Site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

Organizations holds each ministry's public details: its name, minister, biography, media contacts and page links. They appear on the public Ministries page and on each ministry's own page.

The table shows each ministry's Name, Abbreviation, Minister and Active. A ministry left off the public site has a "Not public" badge. If any ministries are inactive, tick Show inactive organizations to list them too.

Core administrators add, deactivate and hand over ministries, and set each one's abbreviation and whether it is public.

Edit a ministry

  1. Choose Edit on the ministry's row. The form opens above the table.
  2. Change what you need:
    • Ministry name (required), and Additional display name, which shows in brackets under the ministry on the Media Contacts page, such as (Child Care).
    • Sort order: a whole number that places the ministry in lists.
    • Minister name, with the title, such as "Honourable Jane Doe" or "Premier Jane Doe". If you leave it empty, the ministry shows no minister.
    • Minister summary and Minister email.
    • Minister photo URL. Upload the photo on Files first, choose Copy public address beside it, then paste the address here. A preview appears once the address starts with https://.
    • Minister biography: shown on the minister's biography page, linked as Read Bio from the ministry page. Clear the biography empties it, and the biography page goes when you save.
    • Meet the Team links: shown as Meet the Team on the ministry page.
    • Under Media contacts: Primary contact and Alternate contact (each with Name, Phone, Cell and Email), and After-hours phone. Phone shows as Direct on the ministry page.
    • Under Ministry page links: Ministry website, Photos (Flickr) address, Videos (YouTube) address, Featured Topics and Featured Services.
  3. Choose Save. You see "Saved. The public ministry pages update within a few minutes."

Cancel closes the form without saving.

The public page shows the alternate contact only when there is a primary contact. The form warns "The public page shows the alternate only with a primary contact."

After you rename the minister, a note warns "The biography still describes the previous minister." Update or clear the biography too.

When a new government takes office, you update every minister's name, photo and biography. When a new government takes office gives the order.

What happens next

  • Saved details reach the public site within a few minutes.
  • Nobody is emailed.
  • Changing a minister here doesn't change their contact record in Media Hub. Update that by hand.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"No changes to save." Nothing in the form changed.
"Enter a ministry name." Ministry name (required) is empty.
"Enter a whole number." Sort order must be a whole number, such as 10.
"Enter the full address, starting with https://, to see a preview." The photo address is incomplete.
"This address didn't load an image. Check that it's the right URL." The photo address doesn't lead to an image. Check it on Files.
"This address points at the Hub, which the public can't open. On Website → Files, use Copy public address and paste that instead." The address was copied from the Hub, so the preview works for you but visitors would get a broken image. Copy the photo's public address on Files and paste it instead.

editor-overview.html:
Who this is for: Release editors (NRMS.Editor).

You write news releases, stories, factsheets and media advisories, approve them, and publish them now or at a set time. Publishing puts a release on the public news site and emails the subscribers and media lists it is meant for.

The everyday path

  1. Start a release with New release.
  2. Write it: the text, page details and categories. Save changes saves everything you changed.
  3. Add photos, video and files if it has any.
  4. Approve it, then publish it now or schedule it. Each step asks you to confirm and says who will be emailed.
  5. Correct it, feature it, unpublish it or delete it if you need to.

Who is emailed, and when it goes public sums up what each step does.

What only you can do
