who-gets-which-email.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

Only Active subscribers get news email. Pending, Disabled and Unsubscribed or deleted subscribers get none.

News releases

Each subscriber chooses lists and a timing. Lists are ministries, sectors, themes and tags. All news covers every release that names a ministry.

Timing What they get
As it happens One email for each matching release, soon after it is published.
Daily digest One email at 5:00 pm BC time listing the matching releases since the last digest. Media advisories are left out. No matching releases means no digest.
As it happens and daily digest Both.
None (media lists only) No news release email. This person is here only for media lists.

A correction to a release never emails anyone again. If a release is unpublished, anything not yet sent is stopped, and daily digests leave it out while it is off the site. If it is published again before 5:00 pm on the day it first went out (the next day if it first went out after 5:00 pm), that digest still carries it.

Emergency alerts

Alerts posted by Emergency Info BC are checked every 5 minutes. A new alert goes at once to everyone active on the Emergency Info BC Alerts list, whatever timing they chose. An alert edited later is not sent again.

Media lists

Release editors choose media lists for a release. Each member of those lists gets the full-text media version. A reporter who is also an As it happens subscriber for that release gets one email, the media version, not two.

When a subscriber unsubscribes

Every release, digest, alert and media list email ends with an Unsubscribe link. It opens the Unsubscribe page on the public site, which asks them to confirm with its Unsubscribe button. Opening the link alone changes nothing. Once they confirm, the page says "You're unsubscribed." and their status becomes Unsubscribed or deleted. Some email programs also show their own unsubscribe button, which unsubscribes them at once.

If something goes wrong, the page says so:

What the page says What it means
"We couldn't unsubscribe you. You're still subscribed. Try again in a few minutes." Nothing changed. They can choose Unsubscribe again.
"This unsubscribe link isn't complete. It may have been cut off in your email." The link was cut short, which some email programs do to long links.
"This link has expired." They came from the manage page, and its link lasts only 24 hours.

Each of these also points them to the public Manage Subscription page, where they can ask for a new link by email and unsubscribe from there.

Emails about the subscription itself

People who sign up on the public site get an email asking them to confirm. They have no record here until they do. They also get an email when they ask to change their preferences or address. These emails still go out while sending is paused.

Nothing you do on the Subscribers screens emails the subscriber. Adding, changing, deactivating and deleting are all silent. Tell the person yourself if they need to know.

find-and-change-subscribers.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

Find subscribers lists everyone who has signed up or been added, 50 to a page. From a subscriber's record you change their lists, their address and whether they get email.

Find someone

  1. Type part of their address in Email contains.
  2. To narrow the list, choose a Status.
  3. Choose Search.
  4. Choose an address to open that subscriber's record. Back to results on the record returns you to the same results.

The Status column shows one of these:

Status What it means
Pending Never confirmed. You shouldn't see it: people who sign up on the public site get a record only once they confirm. If one does turn up, it gets nothing and is deleted after 10 days when the retention purge is on.
Active They get the email they chose.
Disabled They get nothing. Staff deactivated them, or their email kept bouncing. Their lists are kept.
Unsubscribed or deleted They get nothing. Only they can subscribe again.

"(needs attention)" after a status means a media list member has a problem to fix on Media lists.

Read a subscriber's record

The record shows Status, Source, Registered and, once they have left, Ended.

  • Disabled — after repeated bounces means bounces disabled them. Disabled — by staff means someone deactivated them.
  • Bounced emails counted (last 15 days) shows how close they are to being disabled. See Bounces.
  • Media lists names the media lists they are on. Change those on Media lists.
  • History lists every change: when, what, who, and details. Adding a Disabled record to a media list also shows "Added to a media list while Disabled. News release email stays off". "Subscriber" means the person did it themselves. "Bounce processing" and "Media Hub sync" are automatic. The most recent 500 entries are shown.

Change their lists or timing

  1. Open their record. Preferences shows for Active and Disabled subscribers.
  2. Tick As it happens, Daily digest, or both.
  3. Under Lists, tick All news, or tick the lists they want. Lists they have that are no longer offered show under No longer offered. They keep those unless you untick them.
  4. Choose Save preferences. You see "Preferences saved."

The change applies to the next email. Nobody is emailed about it.

Change their email address

  1. Open their record.
  2. Enter the address in New email and again in Confirm new email.
  3. Choose Change email. You see "Email address changed. No confirmation email was sent." and the new address shows at the top of the record.

No confirmation email is sent. Links in emails already sent to the old address stop working, except the unsubscribe links.

If the new address once unsubscribed from a media list this person is on, the Hub asks "That address unsubscribed". Choose Change anyway only if they have asked to get media releases there again. It counts as adding them back to those lists.

For a Media Hub contact, the record says "This address is managed in Media Hub. Change it there." The address can't be changed here.

Deactivate or activate someone

  1. Open their record.
  2. Choose Deactivate. The Hub asks "Deactivate this subscriber?" and explains "They receive nothing until activated again. Their lists, including media lists, are kept."
  3. Choose Confirm deactivate. Their status becomes Disabled — by staff.

To bring back a Disabled subscriber, choose Activate. It happens at once, without a question. You see "Activated. Their bounce count starts again."

Delete someone

Delete when a person asks to stop all email, or when a record must be removed.

  1. Open their record.

  2. Choose Delete. The Hub asks "Delete this subscriber?" and explains "They stop receiving email and are removed from every media list. Only they can subscribe again."

  3. Under Why are you deleting them?, choose one:

    • They asked us to stop sending them email: for a person who phoned, wrote or emailed to say stop. The Hub explains "This is kept as their unsubscribe. If anyone adds them to a media list later, the Hub asks first."
    • Something else, such as a duplicate or test record: for cleaning up records.

    If you choose neither, you see "Choose why you’re deleting them." and nothing is deleted.

  4. Choose Confirm delete.

What this does:

  • Their status becomes Unsubscribed or deleted at once. Staff can't undo it, and Add a subscriber refuses their address while the record exists.
  • They are taken off every media list.
  • With They asked us to stop sending them email, it counts as their unsubscribe, as if they had unsubscribed themselves. History shows "Unsubscribed", with "asked staff" under Detail, and "Left a media list", both with your name, and they appear under Left this list on each media list they were on. If anyone later adds them to any media list, the Hub asks "This person unsubscribed" first. This is kept even after the retention purge removes the record. On Recent unsubscribes they show as "Unsubscribed".
  • With Something else, deleting isn't an unsubscribe, so it doesn't by itself make the Hub ask when you add them to a media list later. History shows "Deleted by staff".
  • The record, with their address and history, stays until the retention purge removes it. When the purge is on, it permanently deletes these records 90 days after they ended. See Operations.
  • Nobody is emailed.

A Pending subscriber's record has only Delete.

Change several at once

  1. Search for the subscribers.
  2. Tick the box beside each one. The box in the heading row ticks the whole page.
  3. Choose Activate selected, Deactivate selected or Delete selected. The button shows how many you ticked.
  4. Read the question, then choose Confirm activate, Confirm deactivate or Confirm delete.

Delete selected is always the Something else kind of delete. If a person asked to stop their email, delete them from their own record and choose They asked us to stop sending them email, so it's kept as their unsubscribe.

Only the ticked rows on the page you are looking at are changed. A message such as "1 changed. 1 skipped: already in that state." tells you the result. Rows are skipped when they are already in that state, or when their status doesn't allow it, such as activating someone who unsubscribed.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"The two email addresses don't match." Type the same address in both boxes.
"Another subscriber record already has that address." Choose Open that record to see it. Two records can't share an address.
"This address is managed in Media Hub. Change it there." Update the contact in Media Hub. The nightly Media Hub sync brings the change here.
"Choose As It Happens, Daily Digest, or both." A subscriber with lists needs a timing.
"Choose at least one list, or all news." Tick a list or All news. Only someone on a media list can have no lists here.
"This subscriber's status changed; reload." Someone else changed them. Reload the page.
"Subscriber not found." The record was removed by the retention purge, or the address in your browser is wrong.

add-a-subscriber.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

Add a subscriber signs someone up for news release email on their behalf. Add only people who have asked to receive it.

Add someone

  1. Enter their address in Email and again in Confirm email.
  2. Under Lists, tick All news, or tick the lists they want.
  3. Tick As it happens, Daily digest, or both. As it happens starts ticked.
  4. Choose Add subscriber. Their new record opens.

What happens next

  • They are Active straight away. No confirmation email is sent, and they are not told they were added.
  • They get the next release that matches their lists. See Who gets which email.
  • Their record shows Source "Added by staff", and History shows "Added by staff" with your name.

To put a reporter on a media list, use Media lists instead. See Media lists.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"The two email addresses don't match." Type the same address in both boxes.
"Choose at least one list, or all news." Tick a list or All news.
"Choose As It Happens, Daily Digest, or both." Tick at least one timing.
"That address already has a subscriber record." Choose Open their record. If they are Disabled, activate them there. If they unsubscribed or were deleted, only they can sign up again, on the public site.
"Couldn't load the list of lists. “All news” still works." The lists didn't load. Reload the page, or add them to All news.

lists-and-categories.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

Lists and categories decides which lists people can choose when they subscribe, and the order they see them in. Each list shows how many active subscribers it has.

The categories are Ministries, Sectors, Themes, Tags, Emergency Info BC and Media distribution lists. List names come from elsewhere and can't be changed here:

  • Ministry, sector, theme and tag names are set by Core administrators.
  • Media list names, order and status are set by Core administrators on Media list names. Under Media distribution lists the screen says "Media lists aren't changed here. Core administrators set these on Media list names."

The Offered column shows whether people can choose each list:

Offered What it means
Yes People can choose it.
No You stopped offering it.
No (retired) The list was retired where its name is set, such as a ministry that no longer exists.
No (category not offered) You stopped offering its whole category.
No (media list) A media list. People never choose media lists themselves.

Stop offering a list or a category

  1. Untick Offer and the list's name, such as Offer Seniors, on its row. To stop a whole category, untick Offer and the category's name under its heading.
  2. "Saved" appears beside the box. There is no question first.

The list disappears from the public subscribe page and from the staff Lists choices. People who already have it keep it, and still get its releases.

To offer it again, tick the box again.

Change the order

  1. Choose Move and the list's name with up or down, such as Move Finance up.
  2. You see "Finance moved up."

Categories move the same way, with Move Ministries up and so on. The public subscribe page shows lists in this order.

What happens next

  • Changes apply at once.
  • Nobody's subscription is removed, and nobody is emailed.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"The lists changed while you were looking. They've been reloaded; try again." Someone else changed the order, or a list was added. Try the move again.
"Media lists aren't changed here. Core administrators set these on Media list names." Media lists can't be offered or reordered here.
"Not saved: Couldn't save. Try again." The change didn't save. Try again.

subscriber-media-lists.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

Media lists holds the reporters on each media list. Release editors pick these lists on a release, and every member gets the full-text media version.

The table shows each list's Members, how many Need attention, and its Status. Members counts only the members who get the list's email. Disabled members get nothing, so they aren't counted; the cell then adds, for example, "(and 2 Disabled, who get nothing)". A Retired list can no longer be put on a release. Core administrators add, rename and retire lists on Media list names.

Choose a list's name to open it. Each member shows their Email, their Status (Active or Disabled), their Source and any problem under Needs attention.

Above the members, a line says how many get this list's email, for example "12 members get this list’s email. 2 more are Disabled and get nothing until someone activates them on their record." A Disabled member's Status says "Disabled: gets nothing". Disabled members stay on the list but are sent nothing. To start sending to them again, open their record and choose Activate.

Add a reporter from Media Hub

  1. Open the list.
  2. Under Add from Media Hub, type a name, email or outlet in Name, email or outlet.
  3. Choose Search Media Hub. Each contact shows their addresses, with the preferred one marked.
  4. Choose Add and the address you want. You see "Added to the list."

Add an address by hand

Use this for people who aren't in Media Hub.

  1. Open the list.
  2. Under Add an address by hand, enter the Email address.
  3. Choose Add to list. You see "Added to the list."

If the address is already on the list, you see "[their address] was already on this list." instead. If they were on it but Disabled, adding them again makes them Active for media email, as for any Disabled address (see below), and you see "[their address] was on this list but Disabled; they’re Active again, for media email." If you added them from Media Hub and their record followed a different contact or email, it now follows the one you chose, and the message adds "Their record now follows the Media Hub contact and email you chose."

What adding does

  • The reporter is not emailed. They get the next release sent to this list.
  • A new address gets a record that receives media email only.
  • An address that is already Active keeps its news release email as it was.
  • If the address already has a record that is Disabled or Unsubscribed or deleted, adding makes it Active again, for media email only. As it happens, Daily digest and their news lists are switched off. Media lists they were already on are kept.
  • For a Disabled person, their bounce count starts again, and History shows "Added to a media list while Disabled. News release email stays off", with what was switched off under Detail.
  • When the address was Disabled, you see "Added to the list. Their news release email stays off; open their record to turn it on." instead of "Added to the list."
  • If a Disabled person also wants news release email again, choose open their record in that message. Tick As it happens or Daily digest and their lists, then choose Save preferences.
  • When you add someone, the Hub may ask "This person unsubscribed" and explain "Our records show they left [when]: they unsubscribed, asked staff to stop their email, or left it in the old system. Add them only if they've asked to receive media releases again." It asks only when its records show this address may have unsubscribed since it was last added to this list: from this list, from all News On Demand email, or in the old News On Demand system. Check with them, or with whoever asked you to add them, before you choose Add anyway. Adding them back clears the question for this list, unless they unsubscribe again.

Remove a reporter

  1. Open the list.
  2. Choose Remove and their address on their row. The Hub asks "Remove [their address] from this list?" and explains "If this is their last list and they were added only for media lists, they stop receiving email altogether."
  3. Choose Confirm remove. You see "Removed from the list."

Nobody is emailed. If it was their last list and they were added only for media lists, their status becomes Unsubscribed or deleted. Removing them isn't an unsubscribe, so it doesn't by itself make the Hub ask when you add them back.

Fix a member who needs attention

A flagged member shows the reason under Needs attention:

Reason What happened
Bouncing Their last 10 emails in 15 days all bounced. They are still on the list and still sent email.
Media Hub email removed The address they use was removed from their Media Hub contact.
Media Hub email belongs to another subscriber Media Hub moved them to an address another record already has.
Media Hub email isn't valid Media Hub has an address that isn't a real email address.
Media Hub email opted out of a media list this member is on Media Hub moved them to an address that unsubscribed from one of their lists, so they were kept at their old address.

To fix a bouncing member:

  1. Check with Media Relations that their mailbox works again.
  2. Choose Resolve and their address. The Hub asks "Clear the bouncing flag?"
  3. Choose Clear flag. You see "Resolved. Their bounce count starts again."

To fix a Media Hub problem:

  1. Choose Resolve and their address. Resolve this member shows their Media Hub addresses.
  2. Choose the address to use, then Use this email. You see "Email updated and flag cleared."
  3. Or choose Clear the flag only to keep their current address. For an opted-out address, the next Media Hub sync flags them again. Update the contact in Media Hub instead, or remove them and add them again.

Left this list

This section lists people who left this list, with when they left and whether they are Back on the list. The screen explains "They unsubscribed, asked staff to stop their email, or left it in the old system." Someone you removed from the list, or deleted for another reason, isn't listed. The most recent 200 are shown.

Media Hub sync

Every night, News On Demand picks up changed Media Hub contacts. Media Hub sync shows when it last ran and what it changed.

To run it now, choose Sync with Media Hub now. You see "Sync finished." and its counts. A long sync may stop part-way and carry on at the next scheduled run.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"That isn't a valid email address." Check the address.
"Media Hub isn't responding. Try again, or add the address by hand." Media Hub is down.
"Media Hub isn't set up on this site. Add the address by hand instead." This site has no Media Hub connection.
"That contact or email is no longer in Media Hub." Search Media Hub again.
"A sync is already running. Try again in a few minutes." Wait for the running sync to finish.
"That address belongs to another subscriber. Choose another email, or remove this member." Pick a different address.
"This member changed while you were looking. Close this, and try again." Someone else changed them. Close the box and try again.
"Couldn't remove. Try again." The removal didn't save.

subscriber-reports.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

Reports shows who receives what, who left, and what was sent. Dates and times are BC time.

Report What it shows
Active subscribers by list How many active subscribers each list has now, split by timing. Show members lists the people on one list.
Recent unsubscribes Everyone who unsubscribed, or was deleted by staff, in the last 90 days.
Sends per release For each release or alert published in the dates you choose, the as-it-happens and media list emails.
Daily digest runs Each 5:00 pm digest: how many subscribers and emails.
Distribution sent and bounced Every email sent from any app, by day and sender.

Choose dates

Sends per release, Daily digest runs and Distribution sent and bounced cover the last 30 days at first.

  1. Enter From (BC date) and To (BC date). Up to 92 days at a time.
  2. Choose Show.

Download a CSV

Each report has a Download link for a CSV file that opens in Excel.

These downloads contain email addresses:

  • Download members (CSV) on Active subscribers by list, after you choose Show members.
  • Download list with addresses (CSV) on Recent unsubscribes.

Each address download is recorded with your name and the report, never the addresses. Keep the file only as long as you need it. Subscribers viewers can't download addresses.

Read the numbers

  • Handed off, not bounced counts emails handed to Distribution, the sending service, less bounces. It is not proof of delivery. An email still queued, or one Distribution failed to send, still counts.
  • Not sent means not yet handed off: a send still going out, held while News On Demand sending is paused, failed, or cancelled on Operations.
  • Items in window on Daily digest runs is worked out when you open the report. A release withdrawn since the run no longer counts, so an older run's number can go down.
  • Distribution sent and bounced won't match the other two reports. It counts by the day it sent, has its own Failed column, and counts every bounce. The other reports go by the day the release was published or the digest ran, and count only bounces matched to a news email.
  • Recent unsubscribes doesn't list people disabled by bounces. Find them on Find subscribers with the Disabled status. It does include people who unsubscribed in the old News On Demand, at the dates they left.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Choose a range of 92 days or fewer." Shorten the dates.
"The start date must be on or before the end date." Swap the dates.
"Enter real dates." Check both dates.
"That list doesn't exist any more." The list was removed. Go back to the report.
"Distribution is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes." Only Distribution sent and bounced is affected. The other reports still work.

subscriber-operations.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

Operations stops and starts outgoing email, shows news email that is held or failed, sets who gets the daily bounce summary, and controls the retention purge. Only Subscribers administrators see it.

Pause News On Demand sending

Pause this to hold news email, for example during an election period or while a problem is fixed.

  1. Under News On Demand sending, choose Pause News On Demand sending. The Hub asks "Pause News On Demand sending?" and explains "News On Demand keeps recording releases and building emails but holds them until you resume. Nothing is dropped." and says who is emailed about it.
  2. Choose Confirm pause. You see "News On Demand sending paused." and the section shows Paused.

While paused, no as-it-happens, digest, emergency alert or media list email leaves News On Demand. Confirmation emails to people signing up still go out.

To resume:

  1. Choose Resume News On Demand sending. The Hub asks "Resume News On Demand sending?" and says how much goes out straight away, counted as you open the question, for example "1,205 held emails for 3 releases start going out straight away. The oldest has waited 12 days, since …". When nothing is held, it says "Nothing is held, so nothing goes out straight away."
  2. Choose Confirm resume. You see how much was actually released, for example "News On Demand sending resumed. 1,205 held emails for 3 releases are going out now." To cancel some held email first, choose Cancel instead and use Outgoing news email, below.

Pause Distribution

Distribution is the service that sends email for every app. Pause it only when email from all of them must stop.

  1. Under Distribution, choose Pause Distribution. The Hub asks "Pause Distribution?" and explains "No email goes out from any app, except system notices, until you resume. Queued email is kept." and says who is emailed about it.
  2. Choose Confirm pause. You see "Distribution paused."

System notices still go out while paused. These include sign-up confirmations, manage-subscription links, the bounce summary and the pause emails themselves.

To resume, choose Resume Distribution, then Confirm resume. The Hub warns that queued email starts going out straight away.

Outgoing news email

This section shows news email that hasn't gone out yet, and news email that failed.

While News On Demand sending is paused, it says how much is held, for example "Held while paused: 1,205 emails for 3 releases. The oldest has waited 12 days, since …". The Held news email table has one row per release and type: As it happens, Media list, Emergency alert, Daily digest (one row per daily digest, with how many releases it carries), or Corrected copy to subscribers and Corrected copy to media lists (a corrected release a release editor chose to email again to the people who already got it). Emails counts the active subscribers it would still go to, leaving out anyone an earlier try already reached. Note shows when an email has already been tried and what went wrong.

While sending is running, the section normally says "Nothing is waiting to go out." Anything listed is waiting to be tried again.

Before you resume after a long pause

Everything held goes out when you resume, however old it is. After a long pause, decide first whether old releases should still be sent, and cancel the ones that shouldn't:

  1. Choose Cancel on a release's row, or Cancel all held email.
  2. The Hub asks "Cancel held email?", says how many emails for how many releases won't be sent, and lists each one. If emergency alerts are among them, it adds, for example, "This includes 1 emergency alert."
  3. Choose Cancel held email. You see, for example, "Cancelled 1,200 held emails." If some had already started going out just before the pause, the message adds "Some had already started going out, so they weren’t cancelled." To keep them, choose Keep it.

Each cancel is recorded with your name and the releases and daily digests it cancelled.

Cancelled email is never sent, and this can't be undone. If an editor later unpublishes the release and publishes it again, it is emailed again as a new release. On Sends per release, cancelled as-it-happens and media list emails count as Not sent; a cancelled daily digest is left out of Daily digest runs. You can cancel only while News On Demand sending is paused. If someone resumed it meanwhile, you see "News On Demand sending isn’t paused, so nothing was cancelled. Pause it first."

Failed in the last 30 days

News email that Distribution refused, or that kept failing for 24 hours, is listed under Failed in the last 30 days with how many emails weren't sent and what went wrong. An email held more than 24 hours that then fails to send is not tried again. Failed email isn't sent again by itself: ask technical support to look at the error. When nothing failed, you see "No news email failed in the last 30 days."

Who is told

Each pause and resume emails the operations inbox with your name and the time, and the question says "The operations inbox is emailed." If this site has no operations inbox, nobody is emailed, and the question says "No one is emailed about it." Subscribers are never told.

Bounce summary

The bounce summary is a daily email at 8:00 am listing bounced subscribers. It is sent only when there were bounces. See Bounces for what it contains.

The section shows where it goes now:

  • "Using the server default:" followed by an address means no one has chosen an address here, so the site's own address is used. The box is empty on purpose.
  • "No address is set, so no summary is sent." means nobody gets it.

To send it somewhere else:

  1. Enter the address in Bounce summary email.
  2. Choose Save address. You see "Bounce summary address saved."

To go back to the site's own address, choose Use the server default. You see "Using the server default again." Saving the box empty does the same.

Soft bounces counted as hard

A soft bounce is a temporary failure, such as a full mailbox. Its code starts with 4. Soft bounces never count toward disabling a subscriber, except the codes you list here. Those count like a hard bounce from the next bounce on, never for earlier ones.

  1. Enter codes in Soft codes counted as hard, such as 4.2.2, separated by commas.
  2. Choose Save codes. You see "Soft bounce codes saved."

Leave the box empty to count none.

Emergency alerts feed

This section shows when the Emergency Info BC feed was last checked and how many alerts were new. Nothing here can be changed. A warning means the last check failed; it tries again every 5 minutes by itself.

The first time a feed is read, its alerts are recorded without emailing anyone. Only alerts posted after that are sent.

Retention purge

The retention purge permanently deletes old personal information. Leave it Off until the business has set retention rules.

When on, every night at 3:00 am it deletes:

  • sign-ups that were never confirmed, after 10 days;
  • people who unsubscribed or were deleted more than 90 days ago, with their history and delivery records.

It never deletes subscribers disabled by bounces. When it deletes someone who had left a media list, it keeps that they left the list, without their address, so adding that address back still asks first.

If it ran now, it would delete shows the counts before you turn it on. While it is on, the section also shows how its last run went. While it is off, no last run is shown.

  1. Choose Turn on the retention purge. The Hub asks "Turn on the retention purge?" and says how many subscribers and links the next run deletes "for good, and keeps doing so every night. This can't be undone."
  2. Choose Turn on purge. You see "Retention purge turned on."

Deleted records can't be brought back. To stop it, choose Turn off the retention purge, then Turn off purge. Nothing more is deleted.

Links in sent emails are cleared every night 10 days after they expire, whether the purge is on or off. They stopped working long before.

Records imported from the old system that had already ended are kept until 90 days after the import.

Test bounce upload

This section shows on test sites only, where every email is redirected and real bounces never arrive.

  1. Choose a bounce message file under Bounce message (.eml), or paste it in Or paste the message.
  2. Choose Upload bounce. You see "Uploaded. Bounce processing picks it up within 15 minutes."

If you leave before saving

If you have changes you haven't saved and you go to another screen or choose your browser's Back, the Hub asks "You have unsaved changes on this page. Leave anyway and discard them?" Choose Stay to keep working, or Leave to discard the changes. Closing or reloading the tab gets your browser's own question.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Distribution isn't responding. Nothing changed." Distribution is down. Try again shortly.
"Distribution isn't responding, so its state is unknown. Reload the page shortly." The Hub can't tell whether Distribution is paused.
"Couldn't change it. Nothing changed." The change didn't save. Try again.
"Enter a valid email address." Check the bounce summary address.
"Enter codes like 4.2.2, separated by commas." Only codes starting with 4 can be listed.
"Couldn't save. Try again." The setting didn't save.
"Choose a .eml file or paste a message first." Add a bounce message before uploading.
"That file is over 1 MB." Bounce messages can be up to 1 MB.
"This site doesn't use the test mailbox." Bounces on this site come from the real mailbox.

bounces.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

A bounce is an email that comes back undelivered. A hard bounce means the address doesn't work, such as a mailbox that no longer exists. A soft bounce is temporary, such as a full mailbox.

When a subscriber is disabled

When a subscriber's last 10 emails within 15 days have all hard-bounced, News On Demand acts on its own:

  • A subscriber who is not on any media list is disabled. Their status becomes Disabled — after repeated bounces, and they get nothing more. Their record and lists are kept. The retention purge never deletes them.
  • A media list member is never disabled. They are flagged Bouncing on Media lists and keep being sent email. Tell Media Relations.

A daily digest counts as one email, however many releases it lists. Soft bounces don't count, unless their code is listed under Soft bounces counted as hard on Operations.

A subscriber's record shows Bounced emails counted (last 15 days) once any have bounced.

Bring a bounced subscriber back

  • They can sign up again on the public site. The confirmation email reaching them proves the mailbox works.
  • Or, once you know the mailbox works, open their record and choose Activate. Their bounce count starts again.

For a bouncing media list member, choose Resolve on the list. See Media lists.

The daily bounce summary

The summary is emailed at 8:00 am to the address set on Operations, with the subject "News On Demand - Bounce Manager" and the date. It is sent only when something bounced since the last one.

It has these parts:

Part What to do
Bounce reports processed The totals, including auto-replies and other messages that weren't bounces.
Hard bounces: count toward 10 in 15 days One line per bounce: the address, the code and the outcome, such as recorded, disabled or flagged.
Soft bounces: not counted, usually no action needed Usually nothing to do.
Unrecorded bounces: not counted; check the bounce mailbox Bounces that matched no news email, such as a bounced sign-up confirmation. If an address keeps appearing and the line says "NoD subscriber", find and delete that subscriber.

A line in bold is a media list member. Tell Media Relations each time one appears, even if they are already flagged. The soft and unrecorded parts stop at 500 lines each and say how many more there were; the rest are in the bounce mailbox.

nod-editor-overview.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers editors (NoD.Editor).

You look after the people who get news release email from News On Demand: you find and change subscribers, add them, keep the media lists up to date and download reports.

Subscriber records are personal information. Search for, download and keep addresses only when your work needs them.

What only you can do

Subscribers viewers see the same records, media lists and reports, but can't change anything. These are yours:

Where What you do there Help page
A subscriber's record Change their lists, timing and address. Deactivate, Activate and Delete. Find and change subscribers
Find subscribers Tick several subscribers and activate, deactivate or delete them at once. Find and change subscribers
Add a subscriber Sign someone up without a confirmation email. Add a subscriber
A media list Add and remove reporters, and fix flagged members. Media lists
Media lists Choose Sync with Media Hub now. Media lists
Reports Download the files that contain email addresses. Reports

To see what a Subscribers viewer can see, read the Subscribers viewer manual.

What you can't do

Subscribers administrators decide which lists people can choose, and in what order, on Lists and categories. You can see that screen but not change it. See Lists and categories.

Core administrators add, rename and retire media lists. Ask one if a list is missing or its name is wrong.

Operations

Only Subscribers administrators can use Operations. It pauses and resumes outgoing email and holds the bounce settings. If email needs to stop, ask a Subscribers administrator. The Subscribers administrator manual covers it.

Before you start

  • Who gets which email explains what each subscriber receives and when.
  • Bounces explains how bounced email disables a subscriber.

Nothing you do on the Subscribers screens emails the subscriber. Tell the person yourself if they need to know.

What you see in the side menu

Under Work you see Subscribers. Its tabs are Find subscribers, Add a subscriber, Lists and categories, Media lists and Reports.

You may also see Releases or Calendar if you have a role there. Those have their own manuals.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac use Command (⌘); on Windows use Ctrl.

Keys What it does
⌘K or Ctrl+K On Find subscribers, goes to Email contains.
⌘S or Ctrl+S On a subscriber's record, saves their preferences, the same as Save preferences.

Signing in

Choose Sign in with Microsoft and use your government Microsoft account. You need a Hub account first: if you see "Your account hasn't been set up. Contact an administrator.", ask a Core administrator to add you. Signing out of the Hub doesn't sign you out of Microsoft.

editor-who-gets-which-email.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers editors (NoD.Editor).

Only Active subscribers get news email. Disabled and Unsubscribed or deleted subscribers get none.

News releases

Each subscriber chooses lists and a timing. Lists are ministries, sectors, themes and tags. All news covers every release that names a ministry.

Timing What they get
As it happens One email for each matching release, soon after it is published.
Daily digest One email at 5:00 pm BC time listing the matching releases since the last digest. Media advisories are left out. No matching releases means no digest.
As it happens and daily digest Both.
None (media lists only) No news release email. This person is here only for media lists.

A correction to a release never emails anyone again. If a release is unpublished, anything not yet sent is stopped, and daily digests leave it out while it is off the site. If it is published again before 5:00 pm on the day it first went out (the next day if it first went out after 5:00 pm), that digest still carries it.

Emergency alerts

Alerts posted by Emergency Info BC are checked every 5 minutes. A new alert goes at once to everyone active on the Emergency Info BC Alerts list, whatever timing they chose. An alert edited later is not sent again.

Media lists

Release editors choose media lists for a release. Each member of those lists gets the full-text media version. A reporter who is also an As it happens subscriber for that release gets one email, the media version, not two.

When a subscriber unsubscribes

Every release, digest, alert and media list email ends with an Unsubscribe link. It opens the Unsubscribe page on the public site, which asks them to confirm with its Unsubscribe button. Opening the link alone changes nothing. Once they confirm, the page says "You're unsubscribed." and their status becomes Unsubscribed or deleted. Some email programs also show their own unsubscribe button, which unsubscribes them at once.

If something goes wrong, the page says so:

What the page says What it means
"We couldn't unsubscribe you. You're still subscribed. Try again in a few minutes." Nothing changed. They can choose Unsubscribe again.
"This unsubscribe link isn't complete. It may have been cut off in your email." The link was cut short, which some email programs do to long links.
"This link has expired." They came from the manage page, and its link lasts only 24 hours.

Each of these also points them to the public Manage Subscription page, where they can ask for a new link by email and unsubscribe from there.

Emails about the subscription itself

People who sign up on the public site get an email asking them to confirm. They have no record here until they do, so the Pending choice under Status on Find subscribers finds no one. They also get an email when they ask to change their preferences or address.

Nothing you do on the Subscribers screens emails the subscriber. Adding, changing, deactivating, deleting and media list changes are all silent. Tell the person yourself if they need to know.

A Subscribers administrator can pause News On Demand sending. While it is paused, release, digest, alert and media list email waits, and goes out when they resume. Confirmation emails to people signing up still go out.

editor-find-and-change-subscribers.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers editors (NoD.Editor).

Find subscribers lists everyone who has signed up or been added, 50 to a page, in address order. From a subscriber's record you change their lists, their address and whether they get email.

Find someone

  1. Type part of their address in Email contains.
  2. To narrow the list, choose a Status.
  3. Choose Search.
  4. Choose an address to open that subscriber's record. Back to results on the record returns you to the same results.

The Status column shows one of these:

Status What it means
Active They get the email they chose.
Disabled They get nothing. Staff deactivated them, or their email kept bouncing. Their lists are kept.
Unsubscribed or deleted They get nothing. Only they can subscribe again.
Pending Never confirmed. You shouldn't see it: people who sign up on the public site get a record only once they confirm.

"(needs attention)" after a status means a media list member has a problem to fix on Media lists.

The Timing column shows None (media lists only) for someone who is here only for media lists.

Read a subscriber's record

The record shows Status, Source, Registered and, once they have left, Ended.

  • Disabled — after repeated bounces means bounces disabled them. Disabled — by staff means someone deactivated them.
  • Source says how they came: Signed up themselves, Added by staff, Media Hub contact or Added to a media list by staff.
  • Media lists names the media lists they are on. Change those on Media lists.
  • Bounced emails counted (last 15 days) shows how close they are to being disabled. It appears once an email has bounced. See Bounces.
  • History opens a list of every change: When, What, Who and Detail. "Subscriber" means the person did it themselves. "Bounce processing" and "Media Hub sync" are automatic. "Admin API" means a system tool made the change, not a person using the Hub. Staff changes show the staff member's name. The most recent 500 entries are shown.

Change their lists or timing

  1. Open their record. Preferences shows for Active and Disabled subscribers.
  2. Tick As it happens, Daily digest, or both.
  3. Under Lists, tick All news, or tick the lists they want. Lists they have that are no longer offered show under No longer offered. They keep those unless you untick them.
  4. Choose Save preferences. You see "Preferences saved."

The change applies to the next email. Nobody is emailed about it. Saving doesn't activate a Disabled subscriber; choose Activate for that.

Change their email address

  1. Open their record.
  2. Enter the address in New email and again in Confirm new email.
  3. Choose Change email. You see "Email address changed. No confirmation email was sent." and the new address shows at the top of the record.

What this does:

  • No confirmation email is sent.
  • Links in emails already sent to the old address stop working, such as the link to change preferences. The unsubscribe links in those emails still work.
  • History shows "Email address changed by staff". It doesn't record either address.

If the new address once unsubscribed from a media list this person is on, the Hub asks "That address unsubscribed" and says when. Choose Change anyway only if they have asked to get media releases there again. It counts as adding them back to those lists.

For a Media Hub contact, the record says "This address is managed in Media Hub. Change it there." instead of offering Change email.

Deactivate or activate someone

Deactivate when someone should get nothing for a while, but keep their lists.

  1. Open their record.
  2. Choose Deactivate. The Hub asks "Deactivate this subscriber?" and explains "They receive nothing until activated again. Their lists, including media lists, are kept."
  3. Choose Confirm deactivate. Their status becomes Disabled — by staff.

To bring back a Disabled subscriber, choose Activate. It happens at once, without a question. You see "Activated. Their bounce count starts again." They get the lists and timing shown under Preferences.

Delete someone

Delete when a person asks to stop all email, or when a record must be removed.

  1. Open their record.

  2. Choose Delete. The Hub asks "Delete this subscriber?" and explains "They stop receiving email and are removed from every media list. Only they can subscribe again."

  3. Under Why are you deleting them?, choose one:

    • They asked us to stop sending them email: for a person who phoned, wrote or emailed to say stop. The Hub explains "This is kept as their unsubscribe. If anyone adds them to a media list later, the Hub asks first."
    • Something else, such as a duplicate or test record: for cleaning up records.

    If you choose neither, you see "Choose why you’re deleting them." and nothing is deleted.

  4. Choose Confirm delete. The record shows "Unsubscribed or deleted on" and the date and time.

What this does:

  • Their status becomes Unsubscribed or deleted at once. You can't undo it. Add a subscriber refuses their address while the record exists.
  • They are taken off every media list.
  • With They asked us to stop sending them email, it counts as their unsubscribe, as if they had unsubscribed themselves. History shows "Unsubscribed", with "asked staff" under Detail, and "Left a media list", both with your name, and they appear under Left this list on each media list they were on. If anyone later adds them to any media list, the Hub asks "This person unsubscribed" first. This is kept even after the retention purge removes the record. On Recent unsubscribes they show as "Unsubscribed".
  • With Something else, deleting isn't an unsubscribe, so it doesn't by itself make the Hub ask when you add them to a media list later. History shows "Deleted by staff". See Media lists.
  • The record, with their address and history, stays. When a Subscribers administrator has the retention purge on, it is removed for good 90 days after they ended.
  • Nobody is emailed.

Change several at once

  1. Search for the subscribers.
  2. Tick the box beside each one. The box in the heading row ticks the whole page.
  3. Choose Activate selected, Deactivate selected or Delete selected. The button shows how many you ticked, such as Delete selected (2).
  4. Read the question, then choose Confirm activate, Confirm deactivate or Confirm delete.

Delete selected is always the Something else kind of delete. If a person asked to stop their email, delete them from their own record and choose They asked us to stop sending them email, so it's kept as their unsubscribe.

Only the ticked rows on the page you are looking at are changed. A message such as "1 changed. 1 skipped: already in that state." gives the result. A skipped row isn't an error:

Skipped because What it means
already in that state They were already active, disabled or deleted.
not allowed from their status For example, activating someone who unsubscribed.
no longer exist The record was removed.
couldn't change – try again Something went wrong for that row. Try it again.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"The two email addresses don't match." Type the same address in both boxes.
"Another subscriber record already has that address." Choose Open that record to see it. Two records can't share an address.
"This address is managed in Media Hub. Change it there." Update the contact in Media Hub. The nightly Media Hub sync brings the change here.
"Choose As It Happens, Daily Digest, or both." A subscriber with lists needs a timing.
"Choose at least one list, or all news." Tick a list or All news. Only someone on a media list can have no lists here.
"This subscriber's status changed; reload." Someone else changed them. Reload the page.
"Subscriber not found." The record has been removed for good, or the address in your browser is wrong.

editor-add-a-subscriber.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers editors (NoD.Editor).

Add a subscriber signs someone up for news release email on their behalf. Add only people who have asked to receive it.

Add someone

  1. Enter their address in Email and again in Confirm email.
  2. Under Lists, tick All news, or tick the lists they want.
  3. Tick As it happens, Daily digest, or both. As it happens starts ticked.
  4. Choose Add subscriber. Their new record opens.

What happens next

  • They are Active straight away. No confirmation email is sent, and they are not told they were added.
  • They get the next release that matches their lists. See Who gets which email.
  • Their record shows Source "Added by staff", and History shows "Added by staff" with your name.

To put a reporter on a media list, use Media lists instead. See Media lists.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"The two email addresses don't match." Type the same address in both boxes.
"Choose at least one list, or all news." Tick a list or All news.
"Choose As It Happens, Daily Digest, or both." Tick at least one timing.
"That address already has a subscriber record." Choose Open their record. If they are Disabled, choose Activate there. If they unsubscribed or were deleted, only they can sign up again, on the public site.
"Couldn't load the list of lists. “All news” still works." The lists didn't load. Reload the page, or add them to All news.

editor-media-lists.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers editors (NoD.Editor).

Media lists holds the reporters on each media list. Release editors pick these lists on a release, and every member gets the full-text media version.

The table shows each list's Members, how many Need attention, and its Status. Members counts only the members who get the list's email. Disabled members get nothing, so they aren't counted; the cell then adds, for example, "(and 2 Disabled, who get nothing)". A Retired list can't be put on a release, and nothing is sent to it, even from a release that already had it. Core administrators add, rename and retire lists.

Choose a list's name to open it. Each member shows their Email, their Status (Active or Disabled), their Source (Media Hub, Added by hand or Subscriber) and any problem under Needs attention.

Above the members, a line says how many get this list's email, for example "12 members get this list’s email. 2 more are Disabled and get nothing until someone activates them on their record." A Disabled member's Status says "Disabled: gets nothing". Disabled members stay on the list but are sent nothing. To start sending to them again, open their record and choose Activate.

Add a reporter from Media Hub

  1. Open the list.
  2. Under Add from Media Hub, type a name, email or outlet in Name, email or outlet.
  3. Choose Search Media Hub. Each contact shows their outlet and their addresses, such as "(workplace, preferred)".
  4. Choose Add and the address you want. You see "Added to the list."

Add an address by hand

Use this for people who aren't in Media Hub.

  1. Open the list.
  2. Under Add an address by hand, enter the Email address.
  3. Choose Add to list. You see "Added to the list."

If the address is already on the list, you see "[their address] was already on this list." instead. If they were on it but Disabled, adding them again makes them Active for media email, as for any Disabled address (see below), and you see "[their address] was on this list but Disabled; they’re Active again, for media email." If you added them from Media Hub and their record followed a different contact or email, it now follows the one you chose, and the message adds "Their record now follows the Media Hub contact and email you chose."

What adding does

Nobody is emailed. The reporter gets the next release sent to this list. What else happens depends on the address:

The address What happens
Has no record A new record is made for media email only. Its Source is "Media Hub contact", or "Added to a media list by staff" for an address added by hand.
Is Active They keep their news release email as it was.
Is Disabled See the next section.
Is Unsubscribed or deleted They become Active for media email only. Their timing and news lists are taken off. If they unsubscribed themselves, the Hub may ask first; see below.

Adding a Disabled subscriber

Being added to a media list is not a request for news release email. So when the address is Disabled:

  • They become Active, and get media email only.
  • Their As it happens and Daily digest timing and their news lists are taken off. Media lists they were already on are kept.
  • Their bounce count starts again.
  • History shows "Added to a media list while Disabled. News release email stays off". Detail lists the timing and lists they had.
  • You see "Added to the list. Their news release email stays off; open their record to turn it on." instead of "Added to the list."

If the person has also asked for news release email again:

  1. Choose open their record in that message.
  2. Tick As it happens or Daily digest, and their lists.
  3. Choose Save preferences.

If they unsubscribed

When you add someone, the Hub may ask "This person unsubscribed" and explain "Our records show they left [when]: they unsubscribed, asked staff to stop their email, or left it in the old system. Add them only if they've asked to receive media releases again." It asks only when its records show this address may have unsubscribed since it was last added to this list: from this list, from all News On Demand email, or in the old News On Demand system. Check with them, or with whoever asked you to add them, before you choose Add anyway. Adding them back clears the question for this list, unless they unsubscribe again.

If they haven't asked to get media releases again, choose Cancel.

Remove a reporter

  1. Open the list.
  2. Choose Remove and their address on their row. The Hub asks "Remove [their address] from this list?" and explains "If this is their last list and they were added only for media lists, they stop receiving email altogether."
  3. Choose Confirm remove. You see "Removed from the list."

Nobody is emailed. If it was their last list and they were added only for media lists, their status becomes Unsubscribed or deleted, and History shows "Ended: removed from their last media list". Removing them isn't an unsubscribe, so it doesn't by itself make the Hub ask when you add them back.

Fix a member who needs attention

A flagged member shows the reason under Needs attention:

Reason What happened
Bouncing Their last 10 emails in 15 days all bounced. They are still on the list and still sent email.
Media Hub email removed The address they use was removed from their Media Hub contact.
Media Hub email belongs to another subscriber Media Hub moved them to an address another record already has.
Media Hub email isn't valid Media Hub has an address that isn't a real email address.
Media Hub email opted out of a media list this member is on Media Hub moved them to an address that unsubscribed from one of their lists, so they were kept at their old address.

To fix a bouncing member:

  1. Check with Media Relations that their mailbox works again.
  2. Choose Resolve and their address. The Hub asks "Clear the bouncing flag?" and explains "Do this once their mailbox works again. Their bounce count starts again from now."
  3. Choose Clear flag. You see "Resolved. Their bounce count starts again."

To fix a Media Hub problem:

  1. Choose Resolve and their address. Resolve this member shows their Media Hub addresses under Choose the email to use.
  2. Choose the address to use, then Use this email. You see "Email updated and flag cleared."
  3. Or choose Clear the flag only to keep their current address. You see "Flag cleared."

For Media Hub email opted out of a media list this member is on, Clear the flag only lasts only until the next Media Hub sync, which flags them again. You see "Flag cleared until the next Media Hub sync." To fix it for good, choose another of their addresses, update the contact in Media Hub, or remove them and add them again, confirming the unsubscribe.

Left this list

This section lists people who left this list, with when they left and whether they are Back on the list. The screen explains "They unsubscribed, asked staff to stop their email, or left it in the old system." Someone you removed from the list, or deleted for another reason, isn't listed. The most recent 200 are shown.

Media Hub sync

Every night, News On Demand picks up changed Media Hub contacts. Media Hub sync on Media lists shows when it last ran and what it changed.

To run it now, choose Sync with Media Hub now. You see "Sync finished." and its counts. A long sync may stop part-way: you then see "Sync stopped part-way and carries on at the next scheduled run."

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"That isn't a valid email address." Check the address.
"Media Hub isn't responding. Try again, or add the address by hand." Media Hub is down.
"Media Hub isn't set up on this site. Add the address by hand instead." This site has no Media Hub connection.
"That contact or email is no longer in Media Hub." Search Media Hub again.
"A sync is already running. Try again in a few minutes." Wait for the running sync to finish.
"That address belongs to another subscriber. Choose another email, or remove this member." Pick a different address.
"That address opted out of a media list this member is on. Choose another email, update the contact in Media Hub, or remove them and add them again, confirming the opt-out." The address you chose unsubscribed from one of their lists. Pick a different address.
"This member changed while you were looking. Close this, and try again." Someone else changed them. Close the box and try again.
"Couldn't remove. Try again." The removal didn't save.

editor-subscriber-reports.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers editors (NoD.Editor).

Reports shows who receives what, who left, and what was sent. Dates and times are BC time.

Report What it shows
Active subscribers by list How many active subscribers each list has now, split by timing. Show members lists the people on one list.
Recent unsubscribes Everyone who unsubscribed, or was deleted by staff, in the last 90 days.
Sends per release For each release or alert published in the dates you choose, the as-it-happens and media list emails.
Daily digest runs Each 5:00 pm digest: how many subscribers and emails.
Distribution sent and bounced Every email sent from any app, by day and sender.

Choose dates

Sends per release, Daily digest runs and Distribution sent and bounced cover the last 30 days at first.

  1. Enter From (BC date) and To (BC date). Up to 92 days at a time.
  2. Choose Show.

See who is on a list

  1. Open Active subscribers by list.
  2. Choose Show members on the list's row.
  3. To narrow it, choose a Timing: Any timing, As it happens or Daily digest.

Choose an address to open that subscriber's record.

Download a CSV

Each report has a download link for a CSV file that opens in Excel, such as Download (CSV) or Download counts (CSV).

Two downloads contain email addresses. Only Subscribers editors and administrators can use them:

  • Download members (CSV) on Active subscribers by list, after you choose Show members. It has the members for the timing you chose.
  • Download list with addresses (CSV) on Recent unsubscribes.

Each address download is recorded with your name and the report, never the addresses. Download addresses only when your work needs them, keep the file only as long as you need it, and don't send it on.

Read the numbers

  • Handed off, not bounced counts emails handed to Distribution, the sending service, less bounces. It is not proof of delivery. An email still queued, or one Distribution failed to send, still counts.
  • Not sent means not yet handed off: a send still going out, held while News On Demand sending is paused, failed, or cancelled by a Subscribers administrator.
  • Items in window on Daily digest runs is worked out when you open the report. A release withdrawn since the run no longer counts, so an older run's number can go down.
  • Distribution sent and bounced won't match the other two reports. It counts by the day it sent, has its own Failed column, and counts every bounce. The other reports go by the day the release was published or the digest ran, and count only bounces matched to a news email.

Recent unsubscribes:

  • includes people who unsubscribed in the old News On Demand, at the dates they left;
  • doesn't list people disabled by bounces. Find them on Find subscribers with the Disabled status;
  • doesn't list someone whose status changed because you removed them from their last media list.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Choose a range of 92 days or fewer." Shorten the dates.
"The start date must be on or before the end date." Swap the dates.
"Enter real dates." Check both dates.
"That list doesn't exist any more." The list was removed. Go back to the report.
"Distribution is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes." Only Distribution sent and bounced is affected. The other reports still work.
"Couldn't load the report. Try again." Reload the page.

editor-lists-and-categories.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers editors (NoD.Editor).

Lists and categories shows every list people can subscribe to, how many active subscribers each one has, and whether it is offered. You can look but not change it: Subscribers administrators decide what is offered and in what order.

At the top, All news shows how many active subscribers chose all news. Under each category, such as Ministries or Tags, each list shows Active subscribers and Offered:

Offered What it means
Yes People can choose it on the public site, and you can tick it under Lists on a subscriber's record.
No A Subscribers administrator stopped offering it.
No (retired) The list was retired where its name is set, such as a ministry that no longer exists.
No (category not offered) A Subscribers administrator stopped offering its whole category.
No (media list) A media list. People never choose media lists themselves. Manage its members on Media lists.

A subscriber who already has a list that is no longer offered keeps it, and still gets its releases. On their record it shows under No longer offered.

List names come from elsewhere. Core administrators set the names of ministries, sectors, themes, tags and media lists.

editor-bounces.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers editors (NoD.Editor).

A bounce is an email that comes back undelivered. A hard bounce means the address doesn't work, such as a mailbox that no longer exists. A soft bounce is temporary, such as a full mailbox.

When a subscriber is disabled

When a subscriber's last 10 emails within 15 days have all hard-bounced, News On Demand acts on its own:

  • A subscriber who is not on any media list is disabled. Their status becomes Disabled — after repeated bounces, and they get nothing more. Their record and lists are kept.
  • A media list member is never disabled. They are flagged Bouncing on Media lists and keep being sent media and news release email. Tell Media Relations.

A daily digest counts as one email, however many releases it lists. Soft bounces don't count, unless a Subscribers administrator has chosen to count that kind.

A subscriber's record shows Bounced emails counted (last 15 days) once any have bounced. Their History shows "An email bounced" for each hard bounce. The bounce that reaches the limit shows "Disabled after repeated bounces" or "Flagged: repeated bounces" instead.

Bring a bounced subscriber back

  • They can sign up again on the public site. The confirmation email reaching them proves the mailbox works.
  • Or, once you know the mailbox works, open their record and choose Activate. Their bounce count starts again.

For a bouncing media list member, choose Resolve on the list. See Media lists.

Subscribers administrators choose where the daily bounce summary is emailed.

nod-viewer-overview.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers viewers (NoD.Viewer).

You can look up the people who get news release email from News On Demand: their records, the media lists and the reports. You can't change anything, and you can't download email addresses. If something needs changing, ask a Subscribers editor.

Subscriber records are personal information. Look up addresses only when your work needs them.

What you can do

Where What you do there Help page
Find subscribers Find someone by their address, and open their record and history. Find a subscriber
Media lists See who is on each media list, who left it, and who needs attention. Media lists
Lists and categories See which lists people can choose, and how many active subscribers each has. Lists and categories
Reports See who receives what, who left, and what was sent. Download the counts. Reports

To answer "why isn't this person getting our email?", see Who gets which email.

What you can't do

  • Subscribers editors add subscribers, change their lists, timing and address, and deactivate or delete them. They also add and remove media list members. Their manual is the Subscribers editor manual.
  • Subscribers administrators decide which lists are offered, and pause and resume email on Operations. Their manual is the Subscribers administrator manual.

If you open Add a subscriber or Operations by its address, you see "You don’t have permission to add subscribers." or "You don’t have permission to use Operations."

What you see in the side menu

Under Work you see Subscribers. Its tabs are Find subscribers, Lists and categories, Media lists and Reports.

You may also see Releases or Calendar if you have a role there. Those have their own manuals.

Keyboard shortcuts and Help

On Find subscribers, ⌘K on a Mac or Ctrl+K on Windows goes to Email contains.

Help, at the top of every screen, opens the page of this manual for the screen you are on. The Help page also lists the keyboard shortcuts. Shortcuts that save, such as ⌘S or Ctrl+S, do nothing for you on the Subscribers screens.

Signing in

Choose Sign in with Microsoft and use your government Microsoft account. You need a Hub account first: if you see "Your account hasn't been set up. Contact an administrator.", ask a Core administrator to add you. Signing out of the Hub doesn't sign you out of Microsoft.

  • Media lists: release editors choose media lists for a release, and each member gets the full-text media version. A reporter who is also an As it happens subscriber for that release gets one email, not two.
  • A correction to a release never emails anyone again.
  • A Subscribers administrator can pause sending. While it is paused, email waits and goes out when they resume.

Nothing staff do on the Subscribers screens emails the subscriber.

nod-viewer-media-lists.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers viewers (NoD.Viewer).

Media lists holds the reporters on each media list. Release editors pick these lists on a release, and every member gets the full-text media version.

The table shows each list's Members, how many Need attention, and its Status. Members counts only the members who get the list's email. Disabled members get nothing, so they aren't counted; the cell then adds, for example, "(and 2 Disabled, who get nothing)". A Retired list can't be put on a release, and nothing is sent to it.

See who is on a list

  1. Choose a list's name. The list opens.
  2. Read the members. Each shows their Email, their Status, their Source (Media Hub, Added by hand or Subscriber) and any problem under Needs attention. A line above the members says how many get this list's email. A member whose Status says "Disabled: gets nothing" is on the list but is sent nothing until an editor activates them on their record.
  3. Choose an address to open that subscriber's record.

All media lists takes you back.

Needs attention

Reason What happened
Bouncing Their last 10 emails in 15 days all bounced. They are still on the list and still sent email.
Media Hub email removed The address they use was removed from their Media Hub contact.
Media Hub email belongs to another subscriber Media Hub moved them to an address another record already has.
Media Hub email isn't valid Media Hub has an address that isn't a real email address.
Media Hub email opted out of a media list this member is on Media Hub moved them to an address that unsubscribed from one of their lists, so they were kept at their old address.

Subscribers editors fix these. Tell one, or Media Relations for a bouncing reporter.

Left this list

This section lists people who left the list, with when they left (Left) and whether they are Back on the list. The screen explains "They unsubscribed, or left it in the old system." Someone removed by staff in the Hub isn't listed. If more than 200 have left, you see "Showing the most recent 200."

Media Hub sync

Every night, News On Demand picks up changed Media Hub contacts. Media Hub sync, at the bottom of Media lists, shows when it last ran and what it changed, such as "60 changed contacts: 0 updated, 0 flagged, 0 removed, 0 skipped." Subscribers editors can run it sooner.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Couldn't load media lists." or "Couldn't load this media list." Reload the page.
"There's no media list with that key." The address in your browser is wrong. Go back to Media lists.

nod-viewer-reports.html:
Who this is for: Subscribers viewers (NoD.Viewer).

Reports shows who receives what, who left, and what was sent. Dates and times are BC time.

Report What it shows
Active subscribers by list How many active subscribers each list has now, split by timing. Show members lists the people on one list.
Recent unsubscribes Everyone who unsubscribed, or was deleted by staff, in the last 90 days.
Sends per release For each release or alert published in the dates you choose, the as-it-happens and media list emails.
Daily digest runs Each 5:00 pm digest: how many subscribers and emails.
Distribution sent and bounced Every email sent from any app, by day and sender.

Choose dates

Sends per release, Daily digest runs and Distribution sent and bounced cover the last 30 days at first.

  1. Enter From (BC date) and To (BC date). Up to 92 days at a time.
  2. Choose Show.

To go back to the last 30 days, clear both dates and choose Show. You can type new dates while a report is still loading.

See who is on a list

  1. Open Active subscribers by list.
  2. Choose Show members on the list's row. The members show below the counts.
  3. To narrow it, choose a Timing: Any timing, As it happens or Daily digest.

Choose an address to open that subscriber's record.

Download a CSV

Each report has a link to download it as a CSV file that opens in Excel, such as Download (CSV), Download counts (CSV) or Download daily counts (CSV).

You can't download email addresses. Reports says "CSV files with email addresses are for News On Demand editors and administrators." If your work needs a file of addresses, ask a Subscribers editor.

Read the numbers

  • Handed off, not bounced counts emails handed to Distribution, the sending service, less bounces. It is not proof of delivery. An email still queued, or one Distribution failed to send, still counts.
  • Not sent means not yet handed off: a send still going out, held while News On Demand sending is paused, failed, or cancelled by a Subscribers administrator.
  • Daily digest emails are counted in Daily digest runs, once for each subscriber, not in Sends per release.
  • Items in window on Daily digest runs is worked out when you open the report. A release withdrawn since the run no longer counts, so an older run's number can go down.
  • Distribution sent and bounced won't match the other two reports. It counts by the day it sent, has its own Failed column, and counts every bounce. The other reports go by the day the release was published or the digest ran, and count only bounces matched to a news email.

Recent unsubscribes:

  • includes people who unsubscribed in the old News On Demand, at the dates they left;
  • doesn't list people disabled by bounces. Find them on Find subscribers with the Disabled status;
  • doesn't list someone whose status changed because staff removed them from their last media list.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Choose a range of 92 days or fewer." Shorten the dates.
"The start date must be on or before the end date." Swap the dates.
"Enter real dates." Check both dates.
"That list doesn't exist any more." The list was removed. Go back to the report.
"Distribution is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes." Only Distribution sent and bounced is affected. The other reports still work.
"Couldn't load the report. Try again." Reload the page.

calendar-admin-overview.html:
Who this is for: Calendar administrators (Calendar.Administrator) and Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin).

You run the Corporate Calendar: who can use it, the choices offered on activities, and which comm contact looks after each activity. If you belong to an HQ organization, you also review what the ministries enter.

Which administrator you are

Your role, and whether one of your ministries is an HQ organization such as GCPE Headquarters, decide what you can do.

  • Administrator: you manage Calendar users and their access. You transfer and delete activities of your own ministries.
  • HQ Administrator: an Administrator or system administrator whose ministries include an HQ organization. You see every ministry's activities, deleted ones included. You review activities, and you can transfer and delete activities of any ministry.
  • System Administrator: everything an Administrator can do, plus every lookup, the Undelivered events tab, and giving the System Administrator role. You can also change the access of HQ staff.

What only you can do

Calendar advanced users, editors and read-only users can't do any of this.

Where What you do there Who can Help page
Calendar access Give or change a person's Calendar role and ministries. Every administrator, with limits. Calendar access
Calendar > Users Keep contact details and comm-contact ranks. Deactivate, reactivate or link people who use only the Calendar. Every administrator. Calendar users
Calendar > Transfer Move every activity of one comm contact to another. Every administrator. HQ Administrators across ministries. Transfer activities
Calendar > Lookups The choices offered on activities, such as HQ tags and event planners. Administrators change 4 lookups. System administrators change all 11. Calendar lookups
Delete on an activity Delete an activity. Every administrator. Delete an activity
The activity list Review selected, deleted activities and the Exec Look Ahead report. HQ Administrators. HQ review
Calendar > Undelivered events Send again activity changes that Releases refused. System administrators. Undelivered events

What you share with other Calendar users

Everyone with Calendar access uses the list, filters, My Queries, Updates, Excel export and the Look Ahead, 30/60/90 and Planning reports. Editors and above create, change and clone their ministries' activities. HQ staff at Editor and above also have Clear LA Status, and HQ staff at Advanced and above also have Corporate Queries, the Confidential filter and Review.

The Calendar advanced user manual, the Calendar editor manual and the Calendar read-only manual cover that work.

Where your changes show up

  • Role, ministry and account changes reach the Calendar within a minute.
  • Activity changes reach Releases within a minute. Release editors who also have Calendar access see confirmed activities with an "Approved" category on the Forecast tab, and can plan a release from them. Confidential and deleted activities never appear there.
  • Nothing in this manual emails anyone.

What you see in the side menu

Under Work you see Calendar. Under Administration you see Calendar access.

The Calendar's tabs are Calendar, Updates, Lookups, Users and Transfer. System administrators also see Undelivered events.

calendar-admin-access.html:
Who this is for: Calendar administrators (Calendar.Administrator) and Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin).

Calendar access, under Administration in the side menu, gives a person a Calendar role and the ministries they work for. Each person has one role or No Calendar access.

The table shows everyone with a Hub account: Name, Email, Calendar role and Ministries. Inactive people are hidden until you tick Show inactive users, including those with no email.

What you can give

  • The roles, lowest to highest, are Read Only, Editor, Advanced, Administrator and System Administrator.
  • Administrators can give any role up to Administrator. Only system administrators can give System Administrator.
  • You can give any ministry, not just your own.
  • HQ organizations are marked "— HQ" in the ministry list. Their members see every ministry in the Calendar. Only HQ Administrators and system administrators are offered them.
  • HQ Administrator isn't a separate role: give Administrator and tick an HQ ministry.

Give or change someone's access

The person needs a Hub account first. Only a Core administrator can add one.

  1. Type part of their name or email in Find a user by name or email.
  2. Choose Edit on their row.
  3. Choose their Calendar role.
  4. Under Ministries, tick every ministry they work for. A role needs at least one ministry.
  5. Choose Save Calendar access. You see "Saved Calendar access for" followed by their name.

Saving replaces the person's whole ministry list with what is ticked.

You can make the same change from the person's page on Calendar > Users: choose Edit Calendar access for followed by their name.

Remove someone's access

  1. Choose Edit on their row.
  2. Choose No Calendar access in Calendar role.
  3. Choose Save Calendar access.

Their activities keep them as comm contact. To hand those activities to someone else, use Transfer activities.

What happens next
