  • The change reaches the Calendar within a minute.
  • A person whose access was removed sees "You don't have Calendar access. Ask a Calendar administrator." on their next click in the Calendar. They stay signed in to the Hub.
  • Release editors see Calendar activities on the Forecast only if they have Calendar access, and only the activities that access lets them see.
  • Nobody is emailed.

When Edit isn't offered

Some rows show a note instead of Edit.

Note What it means
"You can't change your own Calendar access." Ask another administrator or a Core administrator.
"Only a System Administrator or a Core administrator can change this user's access." The person is a system administrator and you are an Administrator.
"Only an HQ Administrator, a System Administrator or a Core administrator can change this user's access." The person belongs to an HQ organization and you don't.
"Only a Core administrator can give Calendar access to an inactive user who has none." The person's Hub account is inactive and has no Calendar role. Ask a Core administrator.

If you have no ministry yourself, the Calendar shows "You aren't in any ministry yet, so there are no activities to show you. Ask another Calendar administrator or a Core administrator to add your ministry." You can't add it yourself.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"choose at least one ministry for a Calendar role" Tick a ministry, or choose No Calendar access.
"Health is no longer active or doesn't exist. Untick it, then save again." The named ministry was deactivated while you were editing. Untick it. A person who already had a deactivated ministry keeps it when you save.

calendar-users.html:
Who this is for: Calendar administrators (Calendar.Administrator) and Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin).

Calendar > Users lists everyone with Calendar access, one row for each of their ministries: Name, Ministry, Comm contact, Calendar role and Active.

  • Type a name or a ministry abbreviation in Find by name or ministry to narrow the list.
  • Tick Show inactive users, including those with no email or Show users without Calendar access to see more people.
  • Choose a name to open that person's page.

If two old Calendar accounts had the same email address, they are now one user.

A person's page has four parts: Calendar access, Contact details, Comm contact and Account. Changes to access and accounts reach the Calendar within a minute. Contact details and ranks take effect at once.

Change their Calendar access

Choose Edit Calendar access for followed by their name. The choices and limits are the same as on Calendar access. Where you can't change their access, the page says why instead.

Contact details

  1. Fill in Phone (up to 20 characters), Mobile (12 digits and hyphens, like 250-555-0100), Job title and Description. Leave any of them empty if you like.
  2. Choose Save contact details. You see "Saved contact details."

The phone number shows under the person's name in the list's Comm Contact column and in the Excel export.

Comm-contact rank

A rank makes the person a comm contact for that ministry, so editors can choose them as an activity's Comm Contact. The page has one Comm contact rank for box for each of their ministries.

  1. Choose a rank: Comm Director, Comm Manager, Sr. PAO, PAO, Jr. PAO or Other.
  2. The rank saves as soon as you choose it. Beside the box you see, for example, "Saved: Comm Director for Health (HLTH)." If it doesn't save, the same place says why, such as "The rank wasn't saved. Try again."

Choose Not a comm contact to stop offering them. Activities that already have them as comm contact keep them, but can't be cloned until they have an active comm contact.

"Give this user a ministry under Calendar access (Edit Calendar access) first." means they have no ministry yet. Choose Edit Calendar access above and give them one.

Just after you give someone a ministry, or take one away, the page says "Updating their ministries in the Calendar… This page catches up by itself in a moment." Stay on the page: the rank boxes follow by themselves, usually within a minute. If they haven't after about a minute and a half, the page says "The Calendar hasn't picked up their ministry changes yet. Reload the page in a minute."

Deactivate someone

Deactivating closes the person's Hub account. It signs them out at once, everywhere in the Hub, and they can't sign in again until reactivated.

  1. Under Account, choose Deactivate followed by their name.
  2. The page lists their Open activities: activities you can see where they are the comm contact, that aren't deleted and haven't ended, even if you set them to Not a comm contact. Only the first 500 are listed.
  3. If they also work for ministries you don't belong to, the page says "They also work for ministries you don't belong to. Ask an HQ Administrator to check and transfer their activities there." You can't see their activities in those ministries, so the page doesn't say whether there are any. With none listed, it says "No open activities in your ministries." instead of "No open activities."
  4. To hand the listed activities over first, choose Transfer their activities first. Transfer opens with them already chosen as From comm contact when they are a comm contact for one ministry; for several, choose which. See Transfer activities.
  5. Choose Deactivate, or Deactivate anyway when activities are listed. You see that the person "is deactivated and signed out. The Calendar's lists catch up within a minute."

Deactivating doesn't move their activities. Each one keeps them as comm contact and can still be saved, but can't be cloned until it has an active comm contact. Editors can't choose them as a comm contact any more.

Nobody is emailed, including the person.

Reactivate someone

Choose Reactivate followed by their name. You see that the person "is reactivated. The Calendar picks this up within a minute." Their ranks come back as they were.

Link someone with no email

People brought in from the old Calendar without an email show "No email — inactive". Their page says "This user was imported without an email. Linking sets their email and activates them."

  1. Enter their work address in Email.
  2. Choose Link and activate. You see that the person "is linked and active. The Calendar picks this up within a minute."

They can then sign in with Microsoft using that address.

Who you can deactivate, reactivate or link

Only people who use nothing in the Hub but the Calendar, and whose Calendar access you could change. You can't deactivate yourself, so the button isn't shown on your own page.

For anyone else you can't change, Account says why instead of showing the button. The message names the button it replaces: deactivate, reactivate or link.

Message What it means
"Only a Core administrator can deactivate someone who also has other Hub roles." The person also works in Releases or Subscribers. Ask a Core administrator.
"Only a Core administrator can reactivate someone who has no Calendar role." The person has no Calendar role. Ask a Core administrator.
"Only an HQ Administrator, a System Administrator or a Core administrator can deactivate someone in an HQ organization." The person belongs to an HQ organization and you don't.
"Only a System Administrator or a Core administrator can deactivate a System Administrator." The person is a system administrator and you are an Administrator.

If the person's access changed a moment ago, the same message can appear after you choose the button instead.

If you leave before saving

If you have changes you haven't saved and you go to another screen or choose your browser's Back, the Hub asks "You have unsaved changes on this page. Leave anyway and discard them?" Choose Stay to keep working, or Leave to discard the changes. Closing or reloading the tab gets your browser's own question.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"at most 20 characters" Shorten the phone number.
"use 12 digits and hyphens, like 250-555-0100" Fix the mobile number, or leave it empty.
"job title: at most 100 characters" Shorten the job title.
"description: at most 2000 characters" Shorten the description.
"Health isn't one of this user's ministries in the Calendar yet. Save their ministries first." That ministry was only just given, or taken away, in another window. Reload the page, and choose the rank again once its box appears.
"A user with that email already exists." When linking: another Hub account has that address. Ask a Core administrator.
"This user isn't in the Calendar." The address you opened isn't a Calendar user. Go back to All Calendar users.

calendar-transfer.html:
Who this is for: Calendar administrators (Calendar.Administrator) and Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin).

Calendar > Transfer moves every activity of one comm contact to another, past ones included. Use it when someone leaves or changes jobs. Deleted activities stay where they are.

Move the activities

  1. Choose From comm contact. Contacts who are no longer active, or whose account is inactive, are marked "— inactive". If you came from Transfer their activities first on a user's page, that person is already chosen when they are a comm contact for one ministry.
  2. Choose To comm contact. Only active contacts whose ministry can lead an activity are offered.
  3. Choose Preview. You see how many will move, such as "4 activities will move from Robin Example (HLTH) to Sam Example (FIN). Their lead ministry becomes Finance."
  4. Choose Transfer 4 activities (the button names the count). You see "Transferred 4 activities from Robin Example (HLTH) to Sam Example (FIN)."

Nothing asks you again: the preview is your check. Changing either list clears the preview.

Which activities move

  • HQ Administrators: both lists show every ministry's comm contacts. Every activity of the first contact moves.
  • Other administrators, system administrators included: both lists show only your own ministries' comm contacts. Only activities led by the first contact's ministry move. An activity another ministry leads and only shares with yours stays where it is.

What changes on each activity

  • Its Comm Contact becomes the new contact, and its Lead Ministry becomes the new contact's ministry.
  • When the lead ministry changes, the old ministry's staff can no longer change the activity. They no longer see it at all unless it is shared with their ministry.
  • Its status, its review marks and its "updated" time don't change. HQ is not asked to review it again.
  • Its View changes records that you transferred it, with the old and new comm contact and lead ministry. Transfers don't appear on Updates.
  • Anyone editing one of these activities at the time is told someone else changed it when they save, and must reload.
  • Transfer works during the daily change freeze.
  • Nobody is emailed.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Choose two different comm contacts" From and To are the same contact.
"Choose an active comm contact to transfer to" The To contact was made inactive. Choose another.
"That person's account is inactive" The To person was deactivated. Choose another.
"That ministry is no longer active" The To contact's ministry was deactivated.
"That ministry can't lead an activity" The To contact's ministry can't lead activities. Choose a contact in another ministry.
"That comm contact is no longer available: reload the page." A contact changed since the page loaded. Reload and choose again.
"Only 100 activities moved from … before a later batch failed. Preview again and try the rest." Some activities moved and the rest didn't. Choose Preview again to see what is left, then transfer again.

calendar-lookups.html:
Who this is for: Calendar administrators (Calendar.Administrator) and Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin).

Calendar > Lookups holds the choices offered on activities, such as categories, cities and HQ tags. Choose a lookup to see its rows. Rows are never deleted: you stop offering a row by making it inactive.

Who can change which lookup

Lookup Extra boxes Who can change it
Event planners Phone, Job title Every administrator
HQ initiatives Short name Every administrator
HQ tags none Every administrator
Digital (videographers) Job title Every administrator
Categories, Cities, Comm materials, NR distributions, NR origins, Premier requested none System administrators
Government representatives Description System administrators

For Administrators, the system administrators' lookups are marked "(read only)" and say, for example, "Only a System Administrator can change categories."

Changes show on activities the next time someone opens one.

Add a row

  1. Open the lookup.
  2. Under Add, such as Add an HQ tag, type the Name and any extra boxes.
  3. Choose Add. You see "Added" and the name.

A new row goes to the end of the list.

Editors also add HQ tags by typing a new one in an activity's HQ Tags. It then appears here too.

Change or stop offering a row

  1. Choose Edit followed by the row's name.
  2. Change the name or the extra boxes.
  3. To stop offering it, untick Active. To offer it again, tick it.
  4. Choose Save. You see "Saved" and the name.

An inactive row shows Inactive under Status. Activities that already have it keep it. Nobody can choose it for another activity.

Renaming a row renames it on every activity that has it.

Change the order

Choose Move followed by the row's name and up or down. You see, for example, "Moved Housing up." Activities offer the rows in this order.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"an active row with that name already exists" Two active rows can't share a name, whatever the capitals. Use the existing row, or make it inactive first. The same applies when you make an inactive row active again.
"enter a name" The name is empty.
"at most 50 characters" The name is too long. The limit depends on the lookup, from 50 to 255 characters.
"Phone: at most 50 characters" Shorten the phone number.
"Job title: at most 150 characters" Shorten the job title.
"Short name: at most 40 characters" Shorten the short name.
"Description: at most 84 characters" Shorten the description.
"the list changed since you loaded it: reload and try again" Someone else added a row while you were moving one. Reload the page.

calendar-delete-activity.html:
Who this is for: Calendar administrators (Calendar.Administrator) and Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin).

Only administrators see Delete on an activity. You can delete an activity your ministry leads. HQ Administrators can delete any activity. A ministry that is only shared on an activity can't delete it.

Delete an activity

  1. Open the activity from the list.
  2. Choose Delete. The Hub asks, for example, "Delete HLTH-2?" and explains "It leaves the list for everyone but HQ Administrators, who can review the deletion. Any unsaved changes are discarded."
  3. Choose Delete. You are back on the list and see "Deleted HLTH-2."

What happens next

  • The activity leaves the list, Updates and the Excel export for everyone except HQ Administrators, and leaves every PDF report. Unless you are an HQ Administrator, you can't open it again either.
  • HQ Administrators see it struck through in the list, waiting for them to review the deletion. See HQ review.
  • It leaves the Forecast in Releases, and no release can be linked to it from then on.
  • A deletion can't be undone. To bring an activity back, create it again.
  • Nobody is emailed.

When Delete isn't offered

  • The activity is led by another ministry, or only shared with yours.
  • It is during the daily change freeze, and you aren't in an HQ organization. The page shows the freeze message.
  • Someone else is editing it.
  • It is already deleted.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Someone else changed this activity — reload to see their changes" Someone saved it after you opened it. Choose Reload, check it, then delete.
"This activity is deleted" Someone deleted it first.
"This activity is no longer available." It was deleted, or moved out of your ministries, after you opened it.

calendar-hq-review.html:
Who this is for: Calendar administrators (Calendar.Administrator) and Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin) who belong to an HQ organization.

HQ reviews what the ministries enter. This page is for HQ Administrators: Administrators and system administrators whose ministries include an HQ organization. Review and Corporate Queries are shared with HQ advanced users. Review selected, deleted activities and the Exec Look Ahead are yours alone.

What you see

  • Every ministry's activities, confidential ones included.
  • Cells changed since the last review are shaded in the list. Screen readers hear "(changed, needs review)".
  • Deleted activities. A deletion waiting for your review shows struck through in the list while the filter's Status is Any status or Changed. On Updates, its lines are marked "(deleted)".

Review one activity

  1. Open the activity from the list.
  2. Choose Review. You are back on the list and see, for example, "Reviewed HLTH-1."

Review marks the activity Reviewed and clears its "changed" marks. If you have unsaved changes, save or cancel them first; the page says "Save or cancel your changes to review or clone, or choose Save and review." Save and review saves them and reviews in one step.

Save and review

When you change an activity yourself, your save marks your own changes "Changed: needs review". Save and review, beside Save, saves your changes and then marks the activity Reviewed, as Save followed by Review would. You are back on the list and see, for example, "Saved and reviewed HLTH-1." ⌘S or Ctrl+S is still a plain Save.

  • If the save finds a problem, nothing is reviewed and your changes stay on screen.
  • If the save works but the review doesn't, the activity stays saved and open, and the page says so, for example "Saved HLTH-1, but it wasn't marked reviewed: someone changed it in between. Reload to see their change, then choose Review."

Review a deletion

A deleted activity opens read-only and says "This activity is deleted. HQ Administrators can review the deletion; nothing else can change it." Its only action is Review.

Reviewing it takes it off the list's default view. The activity stays deleted. A corporate query with Deleted ticked still finds it.

Review several at once

  1. In the list, tick the box beside each activity number, such as Select HLTH-1.
  2. Choose Review selected, beside New activity. The button shows how many are ticked, up to 500 at a time.
  3. The Hub asks first, for example "Review 3 activities?": "Their “Changed: needs review” marks are cleared and they become Reviewed. This can’t be undone." Choose Review, or Cancel to review nothing.
  4. You see, for example, "Reviewed 3 activities."

An activity someone changed after your list loaded is skipped, and named: "1 skipped because it changed since the list loaded: HLTH-2." Open it, check the change, and review it again.

If you see "Only 100 of 300 activities were reviewed before a later batch failed", tick the rest and choose Review selected again.

Corporate Queries

A corporate query lists every ministry's upcoming activities by status. It replaces your filter while it runs.

  1. Open Saved views.
  2. Under Corporate Queries, choose Show all or For the next a number of days.
  3. Under With status of, tick New, Changed, Reviewed, Deleted, LA New or LA Changed.
  4. Choose Run corporate query. The list says "Showing a corporate query." with what it shows.
  5. Choose Back to the filter to return to your own filter.

Changed also finds deletions waiting for review. Deleted finds every deletion, reviewed or not.

The Confidential filter above the list (the old Calendar's Look Ahead filter) narrows it to Not confidential only or Confidential only. Show All turns it off. The line beside Filters names the choice while it is on.

Exec Look Ahead

The Exec Look Ahead is a PDF report only HQ Administrators can make.

  1. Set the list's filter to the dates and activities you want.
  2. Open Export and reports.
  3. Choose Exec Look Ahead. You see "Preparing your Exec Look Ahead report…" and then "The Exec Look Ahead report has downloaded."

Each activity shows its title, summary, significance, city and venue, and when it was last updated. With no To date the report covers one month and adds the Long Term Outlook. Deleted activities are never in it.

The report is marked "DRAFT ONLY - NOT FOR CIRCULATION". Share it only with people who may see every ministry's plans.

calendar-undelivered-events.html:
Who this is for: Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin).

Calendar > Undelivered events lists activity changes the Calendar couldn't send to another app for 24 hours. Only system administrators see this tab.

The Calendar sends every new, changed or deleted activity to Releases. Releases uses it for the Forecast, for linking a release to an activity, and for the activity details a new release fills in. While a change is undelivered, Releases still shows that activity as it was before.

"Nothing is waiting: every event was delivered." means all is well.

What the table shows

The newest are first. "Only the 200 most recent are listed." means there are more.

Column What it shows
Event What happened: "New activity", "Activity changed" or "Activity deleted".
About Which activity, such as HLTH-12. An activity you can't see in the Calendar shows only its number, such as "Activity 12".
To The app that didn't accept it, such as Releases.
Attempts How many times the Calendar tried.
Last error The last reason it failed, such as HTTP 503.
Queued When the change was made, in BC time.

The table never shows an activity's own text.

Send one again

Before you retry, check that Releases is working, or ask your operations team.

  1. Choose Retry on its row. The button shows "Retrying…" until the Calendar answers.
  2. You see "Queued for delivery again." and the row leaves the table. The Calendar tries once more within the next minute.

If it fails again, it comes straight back to the table, without another 24 hours of tries. Reload the page after a minute to check. If it is back, Releases is still refusing it: have that fixed before you retry again.

Retrying an old change is safe. If a newer change to the same activity has already reached Releases, the newer one stays.

calendar-advanced-overview.html:
Who this is for: Calendar advanced users (Calendar.Advanced).

You plan the Corporate Calendar: the government-wide schedule of announcements and events. You add and change activities, follow what changed on Updates, and make reports.

Ministry or HQ

Whether one of your ministries is an HQ organization, such as GCPE Headquarters, decides what you can do.

  • In a ministry: you see your ministries' activities and the activities shared with them. You add and change your ministries' activities. You can do exactly what a Calendar editor can.
  • In an HQ organization: you see every ministry's activities, including those marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead). You add and change any ministry's activities, and the daily change freeze doesn't stop you. You also review activities and run corporate queries.

What you can do that editors and read-only users can't

Calendar read-only users look at activities, Updates and reports, but can't add or change anything. Calendar editors add and change activities as you do.

In an HQ organization, Advanced gives you four things that HQ editors don't have:

Where What you do there Help page
The list, Updates, reports and activities See other ministries' activities marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead). The activity list
Saved views > Corporate Queries List every ministry's upcoming activities by status. HQ review and corporate queries
Confidential filter, above the list Show only the confidential activities, or only those that aren't. HQ review and corporate queries
Review, on an activity Mark the activity reviewed. HQ review and corporate queries

In a ministry that isn't HQ, Advanced gives you nothing more than Editor.

To see what the others can do, read the Calendar editor manual and the Calendar read-only manual.

What you can't do

Ask a Calendar administrator to:

  • delete an activity;
  • give or change someone's Calendar access;
  • change the choices offered on activities, such as categories, cities and HQ tags;
  • move activities from one comm contact to another.

HQ Administrators also review deletions, review many activities at once and make the Exec Look Ahead report. The Calendar administrator manual covers this work.

Your help pages

Page What it covers
The activity list Filters, saved queries, columns, Month and Week, the watchlist and the Excel export.
Updates Recent changes to the activities you can see.
Add or change an activity New activity, Save, Clone, files and View changes.
Activity fields What each field is for, and which ones you must fill in.
The edit lock and the daily change freeze When an activity opens read-only, and why.
HQ review and corporate queries The HQ tools.
Reports The Look Ahead, 30/60/90 and Planning reports.
Releases and the Forecast How activities and news releases are linked.

Who sees an activity

  • Its lead ministry, and every ministry ticked in Shared With, see it.
  • HQ organizations see every ministry's activities.
  • An activity marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead) is seen only by its lead and shared ministries, and by HQ advanced users and HQ Administrators. HQ editors don't see other ministries' ones.
  • Only the lead ministry and HQ can change an activity. A ministry it is only shared with can open it but not change it.
  • A deleted activity leaves the Calendar for everyone except HQ Administrators.

What you see in the side menu

Under Work you see Calendar. Its tabs are Calendar and Updates.

You may also see Releases or Subscribers if you have a role there. Those have their own manuals.

When the list is empty

"You aren't in any ministry yet, so there are no activities to show you. Ask a Calendar administrator." means your Calendar access has no ministry. A Calendar administrator adds it.

"You don't have Calendar access. Ask a Calendar administrator." means your Calendar access was removed. You stay signed in to the Hub.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac use Command (⌘); on Windows use Ctrl.

Keys What it does
⌘K or Ctrl+K On the activity list, opens Filters and goes to Search for.
⌘S or Ctrl+S On an activity, saves it, the same as Save.
⌘Enter or Ctrl+Enter On a new activity, saves it.

Signing in

Choose Sign in with Microsoft and use your government Microsoft account. You need a Hub account first: if you see "Your account hasn't been set up. Contact an administrator.", ask a Core administrator to add you. Signing out of the Hub doesn't sign you out of Microsoft.

calendar-advanced-list.html:
Who this is for: Calendar advanced users (Calendar.Advanced).

Calendar lists the activities you can see, from today on, earliest first. The first 30 show. More load as you scroll down, or when you choose Show more (the button names how many).

Two kinds of activity are left out until you ask for them:

  • Awareness dates. Choose Awareness Day / Week / Month in Category to see them.
  • Activities led by the consultations ministry, shown as CITENG. To see them, choose a ministry in Lead Ministry: in a ministry, choose your own (this also lists activities shared with it); in an HQ organization, choose CITENG.

Both kinds always show under My Watchlist Only.

Read the list

  • Choose an activity's title to open it. When you come back, its row is brought into view.
  • The Activity Id column shows the ministry and number, such as HLTH-12. It also shows Reviewed when HQ has reviewed the activity, Shared when it is shared with other ministries, and Release when a news release is linked to it.
  • Under the title you see when it was last updated, by whom, and when it was created.
  • Confidential (not for Look Ahead) under Categories marks a confidential activity. See Who sees an activity.
  • Point at the date to see the scheduling considerations, at the title to see the significance, and at Comm Materials to see the origin and distribution.
  • Choose a column heading to sort by it, except Premier Requested. Choose it again to reverse the order.
  • What the column names mean, under the list, explains the short names.

Filter the list

  1. Open Filters. The line beside it shows the filter in use, or "No filters".
  2. Fill in what you want. You can use From, To, This day only, Search for, HQ Tags, Issue, Dates Confirmed, Status, Category, Lead Ministry, Comm Contact, Representative, HQ Initiatives & Leads, Premier Requested and Distribution.
  3. Under Display, choose Show All, My Ministries' Activities Only, My Activities Only or My Watchlist Only.
  4. Choose Apply filters.

What some choices do:

  • Search for takes an activity number, such as HLTH-12345, or words in the title, summary, city and other text. An activity number finds that activity whatever the other filters and dates say. A plain number without the ministry counts as an activity number only above 10,000; a smaller one, such as a year, is searched as a word.
  • Lead Ministry also finds activities shared with that ministry.
  • My Ministries' Activities Only shows activities your ministries lead, not those only shared with them.
  • My Activities Only shows activities where you are the comm contact.
  • My Watchlist Only shows the activities you have starred.

Reset empties the filter. Choose Apply filters to run it.

The Hub keeps your Display choice for next time. To share a filtered list, copy the page address. If the link uses HQ tools you don't have, the list opens without them.

Save a filter

Under Saved views, My Queries keeps filters you use often. Only you see them.

  1. Set the filter and choose Apply filters.
  2. Open Saved views.
  3. Type a name in Name for this query.
  4. Choose Save this filter as a query. You see, for example, "Saved the query “My week”."

A query saves the filter the list is running. While Filters has changes you haven't applied, Save this filter as a query waits and says "Apply filters first". Display isn't saved with a query.

To run a saved filter, choose its name. Saved views then shows, for example, "Running “My week”". Each query also has Rename, Up, Down and Delete.

"Your queries changed in another tab, so they were reloaded." means you changed them somewhere else. Try again.

Columns

  1. Choose Columns.
  2. Tick or untick the columns under Show these columns.

The Hub keeps your choice for next time. Activity Id always shows. At first, HQ Tags, Lead Ministry, Status and Translations are hidden.

Month and Week

Choose Month or Week to see the same filter as a calendar. An activity that runs several days shows on each of them. Use Previous month, Today and Next month (or Previous week and Next week) to move. Choose List to go back.

At most 1,000 activities fit. "Only the first 1,000 activities are shown. Narrow the filter to see the rest." means there are more.

Watch an activity

Choose the star beside an activity to add it to your watchlist. Choose it again to remove it. Point at the star to see who else watches it, or "Nobody watches this yet".

Use My Watchlist Only in Filters to list your starred activities. The star also works during the daily change freeze.

Excel export

  1. Choose Export and reports. Check the filter it says it will use, such as "Uses your list filter: none (every activity you can see)."
  2. Choose Excel export. A spreadsheet of the activities your filter finds downloads, up to 10,000.
Message What it means
"More than 10,000 activities match: narrow the filter and export again" Narrow the dates or the filter.
"Other exports are running: try again in a few seconds" Wait a moment and try again.

For the PDF reports in the same panel, see Reports.

The freeze line

"Daily change freeze." at the top of the list says when no changes can be made. While the freeze applies to you, it shows as a Change freeze warning and New activity is hidden. See The edit lock and the daily change freeze.

HQ tools

If you are in an HQ organization, you also see the Confidential filter, Corporate Queries under Saved views, and LA status. See HQ review and corporate queries.

For Review selected, deleted activities, the Exec Look Ahead and other administrator tasks, see the Calendar administrator manual.

Older activities

Activities that ended before the move to this Calendar weren't brought over, except awareness dates. If you need an older one, ask a Calendar administrator.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"From must be on or before To." Fix the dates.
"No activities match." Nothing fits the filter. Widen it, or choose Reset.
"(no longer available)" in a filter box The filter names a choice that was removed. Choose another.
"Couldn't save your list settings." Your column or display choice wasn't kept. Try again.

calendar-advanced-updates.html:
Who this is for: Calendar advanced users (Calendar.Advanced).

Calendar > Updates lists recent changes to the activities you can see, newest first. It opens on Today's updates. Latest 5 updates shows the five newest.

Each line says when, who, and what they did: "added activity", "changed activity", "reviewed activity" or "added new clone". Then come the activity's number, its title and its dates as they are now. Point at the title to see the summary.

Choose the activity's number to open it. Save or Cancel there brings you back to the same updates.

Find older updates

  1. Fill in From and To. From starts at yesterday. Both days are included. Leave either one empty to leave that end open.
  2. To narrow it, choose an Update type: Changed, Added, Deleted, Reviewed or Cloned. Deleted finds nothing for you, since you can't see deleted activities.
  3. To narrow it further, type in Search for: words in the activity's title or summary, or the name of who made the change.
  4. Choose Search.

To see one activity's updates, type its number above 10,000, such as HLTH-20001, in Search for. Shorter numbers, and words like COVID-19, are searched as text.

At most 1,000 updates show at once. "Showing the newest 1,000. Narrow the dates or the search to see older updates." means there were more.

What isn't here

  • Changes from before the new Calendar started. Open the activity and choose View changes: older changes are marked "from legacy log".
  • Transfers between comm contacts, and Clear LA Status. Those show only on the activity's View changes.
  • Activities you can no longer see. When an activity is marked Not for Look Ahead, moved to another ministry or deleted, its updates leave the list for anyone who can't see it now.
  • Changes to the Look Ahead fields, unless you see those fields. In an HQ organization you do.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"From must be on or before To." Fix the dates.
"No updates." Nothing changed in that time, or nothing matches the search.
"Activity not found: it doesn't exist, or you can't see it." Check the number.

calendar-advanced-activity.html:
Who this is for: Calendar advanced users (Calendar.Advanced).

You add activities for your ministries, and change the activities your ministries lead. In an HQ organization you can add and change any ministry's activities. What each field is for is on Activity fields.

Add an activity

  1. On Calendar, choose New activity.
  2. Fill in the fields. The times start at 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM. If you have only one ministry, it is already the Lead Ministry. If you are a comm contact of the lead ministry, you are already its Comm Contact. Choosing another Lead Ministry picks you again where you are one of its comm contacts, until you choose a comm contact yourself. The End date follows the Start date until you set the end date yourself.
  3. Choose Save. You see, for example, "Created HLTH-21." The activity stays open, so you can add files.

New activity is hidden during the daily change freeze, unless you are in an HQ organization.

Change an activity

  1. Open the activity: choose its title in the list or the calendar, or its number on Updates.
  2. Make your changes. As soon as you change something, the activity is yours to edit: anyone else who opens it sees it read-only until you finish.
  3. Choose Save. You are back where you came from and see, for example, "Saved HLTH-21." In an HQ organization you also see Save and review, which saves and marks it reviewed in one step. See HQ review and corporate queries.

Cancel goes back without saving. If you have unsaved changes, the Hub asks "You have unsaved changes to this activity. Leave anyway and discard them?" Choose Stay or Leave.

If Save finds a problem

A box at the top, "Fix these to save", lists each problem. Choose one to go to its field. Nothing is saved until they are fixed.

A start or end date in the past is only a warning: "The start date is in the past." or "The end date is in the past." The activity still saves.

What happens when you save

  • A new activity is New. Saving a change to most fields makes it Changed, until HQ reviews it.
  • HQ sees which fields changed, marked "Changed: needs review".
  • The change reaches Releases within a minute. A release already linked to the activity doesn't change. If a linked release is still to go out and you change a date or time, a warning above Save says so, for example "A release is planned against HLTH-21 (Release 2026HLTH0001: Scheduled, Nov 4, 2026 10:00 AM). Changing the date or time here doesn't move the release. Tell the release editor." The same words follow "Saved HLTH-21." Tell the release editor. See Releases and the Forecast.
  • Every change is kept in View changes.
  • Nobody is emailed.

Activities you can only view

"Your ministry is shared on this activity: you can view it but not change it." means another ministry leads it. The fields are read-only, each checklist shows only what is ticked (or "None"), and the button is Back.

An activity also opens read-only while someone else is editing it, or during the daily change freeze. See The edit lock and the daily change freeze.

Clone an activity

Clone opens New activity filled in from this one, for the same lead ministry and comm contact. Nothing is created until you choose Save.

  1. Open the activity.
  2. Choose Clone. New activity opens with "This is an unsaved copy of HLTH-21. Nothing is created until you choose Save. Cancel leaves no copy behind."
  3. Change what differs, and choose Save. You see, for example, "Cloned HLTH-21 as HLTH-22." The new activity stays open, so you can add files.

Cancel, or leaving the page another way, creates nothing.

The copy starts as New, and its View changes says "created it as a clone", naming the activity it was cloned from. Like any new activity, the copy must have every required field filled in before it saves; an older activity may be missing some. It copies the activity's fields except these:

  • the release date and time are emptied;
  • Internal notes is emptied;
  • News Subscribe is emptied;
  • of the HQ Tags, only "30-60-90" is kept;
  • the Executive Summary is set to "**";
  • files and linked releases stay with the original.

If you have unsaved changes, Clone waits: "Save or cancel your changes to review or clone." Clone isn't offered during the daily change freeze, unless you are in an HQ organization.

Add files

The Records section appears only when it is turned on for your Calendar. When it shows:

  1. Save a new activity first. Until then it says "Save the activity first to add files."
  2. Under Records, choose Add files and pick one or more files.
  3. Each file is added straight away, on its own. You see, for example, "Added 2 files."

A file can be a PDF, a PNG, JPEG or GIF image, a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file, an Outlook message, RTF, text or CSV. Each can be up to 25 MB, and an activity holds up to 50.

A file with the same name as one already attached replaces it, but only after you agree. The Hub asks, for example, "A file named Briefing note.docx is already attached (added Oct 12, 2026 by Pat Smith). Replace it? The old file is deleted." Choose Replace, and you see "Replaced Briefing note.docx." Choose Cancel, and you see "Nothing was added.": none of the files you picked is added.

To remove a file, choose Remove beside it, then Remove again in the "The file is deleted from this activity." box.

Adding or removing a file doesn't touch your unsaved changes to the fields. Like saving, it isn't possible while someone else is editing the activity, or during the daily change freeze unless you are in an HQ organization. A file opens only for people who can see its activity.

View changes

View changes lists every change to the activity, newest first. Each entry says when, who and what they did, such as "changed it", "created it as a clone" (the copy may have been changed before it was saved), "reviewed it", "transferred it" or "cleared its LA status". A table shows each field before and after. Changes brought over from the old Calendar are marked "from legacy log".

Choose Back to the activity to return.

Delete an activity

You can't delete activities, so Delete isn't offered. Ask a Calendar administrator of the lead ministry, or an HQ Administrator.

If your session runs out

If you are signed out while you have unsaved changes, sign in again and open the same activity. It says "Your unsaved changes were restored." Signing out yourself discards them.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"It doesn't exist, or you can't see it." (under "Activity not found") Check the number. The activity may be led by a ministry you're not in, or it was deleted.
"Someone else changed this activity — reload to see their changes" Someone saved it after you opened it. Choose Reload. If you have unsaved changes, it asks "Reload and lose your changes? The activity as it is now replaces them." Choose Reload, then make your change again, or Keep editing.
"This activity is no longer available." It was deleted, or moved out of your ministries, after you opened it.
"This activity is deleted" Someone deleted it while you were editing. Your changes stay on the page but can't be saved.
"You can only choose one of your ministries" Choose one of your own ministries as the Lead Ministry.
"Choose a comm contact of the lead ministry" The comm contact belongs to another ministry. Choose another.
"That comm contact is no longer active" or "That person's account is inactive" Choose another comm contact. An activity that already has them still saves, but can't be cloned.
"That category is no longer in use" Choose another category.
"You can no longer copy the activity this was copied from. Start a new activity instead." The activity you cloned was deleted, or moved out of your ministries, while the copy was open. Choose Cancel, then New activity.
"Couldn't save. Your changes are still here; try again." Something went wrong on the way. Choose Save again.

calendar-advanced-fields.html:
Who this is for: Calendar advanced users (Calendar.Advanced).

An activity's fields are in sections, in this order: Overview, Ministry, Planning, Schedule, Release, Event and, when turned on, Records. In an HQ organization you also see Look Ahead, after Event. A "?" beside a field explains it.

What you must fill in

Fields marked "(required)" must be filled in before you can save:

  • Category, Title, Lead Ministry and Comm Contact;
  • Start date and End date, and both times unless you tick All Day;
  • Summary, Significance and Scheduling considerations. In an HQ organization these three are optional.

A category that is a release, such as Approved Release, also needs Origin, Distribution and at least one Comm Materials. The message says, for example, "Choose the origin: this category is a release".

Overview

Field What to enter
Category The kind of activity. HQ Placeholder is offered only to HQ.
Confidential (not for Look Ahead) Tick it to make the activity confidential. The old Calendar called it Not for Look Ahead. Only its lead and shared ministries, HQ advanced users and HQ Administrators then see it, and it isn't offered on the releases Forecast. A new activity isn't given a Look Ahead section, but ticking it doesn't take away a section the activity already has.
Title Up to 100 characters.
Summary Up to 700 characters.
Issue Tick it if the activity is an issue.
Significance Why it matters. Up to 500 characters.
Lead Organization The organization leading it, when that isn't the lead ministry, such as a partner. Up to 80 characters.
HQ Initiatives & Leads Tick the initiatives it supports.
HQ Tags Type a tag and choose Add tag, or press Enter. Existing tags are suggested as you type. A new tag is created when you save. Up to 20. Choose × beside a tag to remove it.

Ministry

Field What to enter
Lead Ministry One of your ministries. In an HQ organization, any active ministry. Some ministries can't lead activities and aren't offered. Changing it empties Comm Contact if the contact belongs to another ministry.
Cross-Government Tick it for a cross-government activity. It doesn't change who sees the activity.
Shared With Tick the other ministries that should see it. They can open it but not change it.

Planning

Field What to enter
Comm Contact The communications person responsible. Only the active comm contacts of the Lead Ministry, chosen above, are offered.
Key activity Tick it for a key activity.
Strategy Up to 500 characters.
Comm Materials The products planned, such as a news release.
Internal notes Up to 4,000 characters.

Schedule

Field What to enter
All Day Tick it for an all-day activity. It hides the times below it.
Dates Confirmed Tick it once the date is firm. Only confirmed activities are offered on the releases Forecast.
Start date, Start time Times go in 5-minute steps.
End date, End time The end can't be before the start.
Potential Dates A general timeline, like "late June". No numbers, TBC or TBD. Up to 50 characters.
Scheduling considerations Anything that affects the timing. Up to 500 characters.

Release

Some categories, such as TV / Radio and Awareness Day / Week / Month, have no release. For those this section is hidden, and choosing one empties the release date and time.

Field What to enter
Release date, Release time When the news release goes out. Fill in both, or leave both empty: Release time starts at "Choose a time". It can't be after the end date.
Origin, Distribution Where the release comes from, and how widely it goes.
Translations Required The languages needed.
Sectors, Themes, News Subscribe The release's topics. A release editor can copy them into a release.
BC Gov News The news releases linked to this activity. See Releases and the Forecast.

Event

Field What to enter
Premier Requested Whether the Premier was asked to take part, such as Yes, No or Invited.
Representative Who represents government at the activity.
At BC Legislature Tick it if it takes place there.
City, Venue Where it takes place. When you choose the city for places not on the list, Other City appears: type the city there. Venue and Other City take up to 55 characters.
Event Planner, Digital Who plans the event, and the videographer.

Look Ahead

Only HQ sees this section. Other users' saves leave it as it is.

Field What to enter
Executive Summary Shown in HQ's Look Ahead report. Up to 2,000 characters.
LA Status None, New or Changed. HQ's Look Ahead flags the activity NEW or CHANGED.
LA Section Where the activity goes in the Look Ahead. It is worked out from fields above it: Category, Issue, Confidential (not for Look Ahead), Lead Ministry, Comm Materials, Dates Confirmed and the start and end dates. Its hint names them. Choose another section to override it; it then says "Override" and offers Use the inferred section. Awareness dates and activities led by the ministry shown as CITENG keep a fixed section, which can't be overridden.
Long Term Outlook Tick it to list the activity in the Look Ahead's Long Term Outlook.

An activity marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead) whose section is overridden needs an Executive Summary.

For Records, see Add or change an activity.

Choices no longer in use

A choice that has been retired shows "(no longer in use)" when an activity already has it. The activity keeps it. You can't choose it for another activity.

Long text from the old Calendar

Some activities brought over from the old Calendar have longer text than the limits allow. They still save. The limits apply only to text you change.

calendar-advanced-hq.html:
Who this is for: Calendar advanced users (Calendar.Advanced) who belong to an HQ organization.

HQ reviews what the ministries enter. If none of your ministries is an HQ organization, you don't see these tools.

What HQ sees

  • Every ministry's activities, including those marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead).
  • On an activity, each field changed since the last review says "Changed: needs review".
  • The Look Ahead section on every activity. See Activity fields.
  • Search for in the list's Filters also searches the Executive Summary.

You don't see deleted activities. Reviewing deletions is for HQ Administrators.

Review an activity

  1. Open the activity.
  2. Check what changed. View changes shows each change before and after.
  3. Choose Review. You go back to where you opened it, and see, for example, "Reviewed HLTH-21."

Review marks the activity Reviewed and clears its "Changed: needs review" marks. It shows on Updates as "reviewed activity".

If you have unsaved changes, save or cancel them first: the page says "Save or cancel your changes to review or clone." Or choose Save and review: see below.

If you see "Someone else changed this activity — reload to see their changes", choose Reload, check the new change, then choose Review again.

Save and review

When you change an activity yourself, your save marks your own changes "Changed: needs review". Save and review, beside Save, saves your changes and then marks the activity Reviewed, as Save followed by Review would. You go back to where you opened it, and see, for example, "Saved and reviewed HLTH-21." ⌘S or Ctrl+S is still a plain Save.

  • If the save finds a problem, nothing is reviewed and your changes stay on screen.
  • If the save works but the review doesn't, the activity stays saved and open, and the page says so, for example "Saved HLTH-21, but it wasn't marked reviewed: someone changed it in between. Reload to see their change, then choose Review."

You review one activity at a time. Review selected, which reviews many at once from the list, is for HQ Administrators.

Run a corporate query

A corporate query lists every ministry's upcoming activities by status. It replaces your filter while it runs.

  1. Open Saved views.
  2. Under Corporate Queries, choose Show all, or For the next and a number of days. It starts at 8.
  3. Under With status of, tick any of New, Changed, Reviewed, Deleted, LA New and LA Changed. New and Changed start ticked.
  4. Choose Run corporate query. Above the list you see, for example, "Showing a corporate query. Every ministry's activities: next 8 days, New and Changed."
  5. Choose Back to the filter to return to your own filter.

Deleted finds nothing for you, since you can't see deleted activities.

The Confidential filter

The Confidential filter above the list (the old Calendar's Look Ahead filter) narrows the list, and the reports made from it:

  • Not confidential only shows activities that aren't marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead).
  • Confidential only shows only those that are.
  • Show All turns it off.

It works straight away, without Apply filters. While it is on, the line beside Filters names it. A saved query doesn't keep it.

Clear LA Status

HQ editors can do this too. It clears LA New and LA Changed, so the next Look Ahead flags only what is new or changed since.

  1. Choose LA status above the list.
  2. In Days ahead (Clear LA Status), enter a number of days. It starts at 8.
  3. Choose Clear LA Status. The Hub asks, for example, "Clear the LA status of 3 activities?" and explains "Every activity you can see that starts up to 8 days ahead, past ones included, loses its LA New or LA Changed status. Each change is recorded in the activity's history."
  4. Choose Clear LA Status. You see, for example, "Cleared the LA status of 3 activities."

With nothing to clear, you see, for example, "No activities up to 8 days ahead have an LA status to clear."

It doesn't show on Updates. Each activity's View changes says "cleared its LA status".

If you see "The LA status of 2 activities was cleared before a later batch failed. Run Clear LA Status again to finish.", choose Clear LA Status again.

What isn't yours

The Exec Look Ahead report, Review selected and reviewing deletions are for HQ Administrators. Deleting an activity is for Calendar administrators.

calendar-advanced-reports.html:
Who this is for: Calendar advanced users (Calendar.Advanced).

The Look Ahead, 30/60/90 and Planning reports are PDFs of the activities your list's filter finds. They list activities in date order, whatever the list is sorted by.

Make a report

  1. Set the list's filter to the dates and activities you want. See The activity list.
  2. Choose Export and reports. The panel starts by saying which filter it will use, for example "Uses your list filter: Dates: 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-14 · My Watchlist Only." It warns you when something you may not have meant to keep narrows it: a Display choice the list keeps from last time, or an activity number in Search for, which leaves only that activity and ignores the dates and other filters. Change the filter under Filters first if that isn't what you want.
  3. Choose Look Ahead, 30/60/90 or Planning. You see, for example, "Preparing your Look Ahead report…".
  4. Wait a few seconds. The PDF downloads by itself and you see "The Look Ahead report has downloaded."

One report is prepared at a time. If you leave the page before it downloads, make it again.

What each report holds

Report What it shows
Look Ahead Upcoming activities in sections, such as Events, Speeches and Releases, Issues and Reports, and Awareness Dates. With no To date it covers 60 days and adds the Long Term Outlook.
30/60/90 One table for each month, from the start of the From month. With no To date it covers about 90 days.
Planning One line for each activity: its schedule, title and summary, significance and number.
  • Each report says under its heading which filter it used, and the Excel export says it on its last row, below the confidentiality notice, for example "Filter: Dates: 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-14 · Lead Ministry: HLTH", or "Filter: none (every activity you can see)".
  • A report holds only activities you can see. Deleted activities are never in it.
  • Reports include Awareness dates even when the list leaves them out.
  • Each activity number in a report links to the activity in the Hub.
  • Each report is marked "DRAFT AND CONFIDENTIAL". Share it only with people who may see those activities.
  • Reports and the Excel export still mark confidential activities "Not for Look Ahead".

If you are in an HQ organization

  • Your Look Ahead puts each activity in its LA Section, shows its Executive Summary when it has one, and flags it NEW or CHANGED from its LA Status. Its Long Term Outlook lists only activities ticked Long Term Outlook.
  • A corporate query or the Confidential filter also narrows the reports.
  • The Exec Look Ahead report is for HQ Administrators. You don't see it.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"Too many activities match: narrow the filter and run the report again" More than 5,000 activities. Narrow the dates or the filter.
"Too many days in the range: narrow the filter and run the report again" A Look Ahead covers at most a year. Choose a nearer To date.
"Too many months in the range: narrow the filter and run the report again" A 30/60/90 covers at most a year. Choose a nearer To date.
"Too many rows to print: narrow the filter and run the report again" The PDF would be too long. Narrow the filter.
"Other reports are being prepared: try again in a few seconds" Wait a moment and try again.
"The report took too long to prepare: narrow the filter and run it again." Narrow the filter.
"The report couldn't be prepared. Try again." Try again. If it keeps failing, tell your Calendar administrator.

calendar-advanced-releases.html:
Who this is for: Calendar advanced users (Calendar.Advanced).

Release editors plan news releases from Calendar activities in Releases. A release can be linked to an activity, and the activity then shows that release.

BC Gov News on an activity

BC Gov News, at the end of the Release section, lists the releases linked to the activity, or says "No releases are linked to this activity."

Each line gives the release's type, its number when it has one, its status and its date, such as "Release: Draft". The status is Draft, Approved, Scheduled, Published or Failed. It changes within a minute of the change in Releases.

  • A release being corrected or taken down still shows Published until that is done.
  • A deleted release disappears from the list.
  • If you also have a role in Releases, each line opens the release. Otherwise it is plain text.

In the activity list, Release in the Activity Id column means a release is linked.

Which activities release editors see

Release editors see Calendar activities on Releases > Forecast only if they also have Calendar access, and only the activities that access lets them see. An activity appears there when all of these are true:

  • its category starts with "Approved", such as Approved Release;
  • Dates Confirmed is ticked;
  • it isn't marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead);
  • it starts from now on, and isn't deleted;
  • no upcoming release is linked to it yet.

From the Forecast, a release editor can start a release for the activity. The release can copy the activity's start, city, lead and shared ministries, sectors, themes and News Subscribe topics.

What your changes do

  • Your changes reach Releases within a minute.
  • Changing an activity doesn't change a release already linked to it. What was copied into the release stays as it was. Tell the release editor if the release needs to change.
  • Marking an activity Confidential (not for Look Ahead) takes it off the Forecast. A release editor who types its number sees, for example, "Calendar activity 3: its details aren't shown to you."
  • A deleted activity leaves the Forecast, and no release can be linked to it from then on.
  • Nobody is emailed.

calendar-editor-overview.html:
Who this is for: Calendar editors (Calendar.Editor).

You keep your ministry's activities in the Corporate Calendar up to date. The Corporate Calendar is the government-wide plan of announcements and events. You add and change activities, follow what changed on Updates, and make reports.

Ministry or HQ

Whether one of your ministries is an HQ organization, such as GCPE Headquarters, decides what you can do.

  • In a ministry: you see your ministries' activities and the activities shared with them. You add and change your ministries' activities.
  • In an HQ organization: you see every ministry's activities, except other ministries' ones marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead). You add and change any ministry's activities you can see. As an HQ editor, the daily change freeze doesn't stop you. See If you are an HQ editor.

What you can do that read-only users can't

Calendar read-only users see the list, Updates, activities and reports, but can't change anything. These are yours:

Where What you do there Help page
New activity, above the list Add an activity. Add or change an activity
An activity Change it and choose Save. Add or change an activity
Clone, on an activity Make a new activity from it. Add or change an activity
LA status, above the list HQ editors only: clear the Look Ahead's NEW and CHANGED flags. If you are an HQ editor

To see what a read-only user can do, read the Calendar read-only manual.

What you can't do

Ask a Calendar administrator to:

  • delete an activity;
  • give or change someone's Calendar access;
  • change the choices offered on activities, such as categories, cities and HQ tags;
  • move activities from one comm contact to another.

Reviewing activities, corporate queries and the Confidential filter are for HQ advanced users. Their manual is the Calendar advanced user manual. Calendar administrators have the Calendar administrator manual.

Your help pages

Page What it covers
The activity list What sits above the list, filters, saved queries, columns, Month and Week, the watchlist and the Excel export.
Updates Recent changes to the activities you can see.
Add or change an activity New activity, Save, Clone, files and View changes.
Activity fields What each field is for, and which ones you must fill in.
The edit lock and the daily change freeze When an activity opens read-only, and why.
If you are an HQ editor What changes when you are in an HQ organization.
Reports The Look Ahead, 30/60/90 and Planning reports.
Releases and the Forecast How activities and news releases are linked.

Who sees an activity

  • Its lead ministry, and every ministry ticked in Shared With, see it.
  • HQ organizations see every ministry's activities.
  • An activity marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead) is seen only by its lead and shared ministries, and by HQ advanced users and HQ administrators. HQ editors don't see other ministries' ones.
  • Only the lead ministry and HQ can change an activity. A ministry it is only shared with can open it but not change it.
  • A deleted activity leaves the Calendar for everyone except HQ administrators.

What you see in the side menu

Under Work you see Calendar. Its tabs are Calendar and Updates.

You may also see Releases or Subscribers if you have a role there. Those have their own manuals.

When the list is empty

"You aren't in any ministry yet, so there are no activities to show you. Ask a Calendar administrator." means your Calendar access has no ministry. A Calendar administrator adds it.

"You don't have Calendar access. Ask a Calendar administrator." means your Calendar access was removed. You stay signed in to the Hub.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac use Command (⌘); on Windows use Ctrl.

Keys What it does
⌘K or Ctrl+K On the activity list, opens Filters and goes to Search for.
⌘S or Ctrl+S On an activity, saves it, the same as Save.
⌘Enter or Ctrl+Enter On a new activity, saves it.

Signing in

Choose Sign in with Microsoft and use your government Microsoft account. You need a Hub account first: if you see "Your account hasn't been set up. Contact an administrator.", ask a Core administrator to add you. Signing out of the Hub doesn't sign you out of Microsoft.

calendar-editor-list.html:
Who this is for: Calendar editors (Calendar.Editor).

Calendar lists the activities you can see, from today on, earliest first. The first 30 show. More load as you scroll down, or when you choose Show more (the button names how many).

Two kinds of activity are left out until you ask for them:

  • Awareness dates. Choose Awareness Day / Week / Month in Category to see them.
  • Activities led by the consultations ministry, shown as CITENG. To see them, choose a ministry in Lead Ministry: in a ministry, choose your own (this also lists activities shared with it); in an HQ organization, choose CITENG.

Both kinds always show under My Watchlist Only.

What sits above the list

From the top:

  1. The daily change freeze line. See The freeze line below.
  2. Filters and Saved views, which open when you choose them.
  3. New activity, on the left. List, Month and Week, on the right.
  4. Columns and Export and reports. HQ editors also see LA status here.

New activity is hidden during the daily change freeze, unless you are an HQ editor. To add an activity, see Add or change an activity.

Read the list

  • Choose an activity's title to open it. When you come back, its row is brought into view.
  • The Activity Id column shows the ministry and number, such as HLTH-12. It also shows Reviewed when HQ has reviewed the activity, Shared when it is shared with other ministries, and Release when a news release is linked to it.
  • Under the title you see when it was last updated, by whom, and when it was created.
  • Confidential (not for Look Ahead) under Categories marks a confidential activity. See Who sees an activity.
  • Point at the date to see the scheduling considerations, at the title to see the significance, and at Comm Materials to see the origin and distribution.
  • Choose a column heading to sort by it, except Premier Requested. Choose it again to reverse the order.
  • What the column names mean, under the list, explains the short names.

Filter the list

  1. Open Filters. The line beside it shows the filter in use, or "No filters".
  2. Fill in what you want. You can use From, To, This day only, Search for, HQ Tags, Issue, Dates Confirmed, Status, Category, Lead Ministry, Comm Contact, Representative, HQ Initiatives & Leads, Premier Requested and Distribution.
  3. Under Display, choose Show All, My Ministries' Activities Only, My Activities Only or My Watchlist Only.
  4. Choose Apply filters.

What some choices do:

  • Search for takes an activity number, such as HLTH-12345, or words in the title, summary, city and other text. An activity number finds that activity whatever the other filters and dates say. A plain number without the ministry counts as an activity number only above 10,000; a smaller one, such as a year, is searched as a word.
  • Lead Ministry offers your own ministries, or every ministry if you are in an HQ organization. It also finds activities shared with that ministry.
  • My Ministries' Activities Only shows activities your ministries lead, not those only shared with them.
  • My Activities Only shows activities where you are the comm contact.
  • My Watchlist Only shows the activities you have starred.

Reset empties the filter. Choose Apply filters to run it.

The Hub keeps your Display choice for next time. To share a filtered list, copy the page address. If a colleague's link uses HQ tools you don't have, the list opens without them.

Save a filter

Under Saved views, My Queries keeps filters you use often. Only you see them.

  1. Set the filter and choose Apply filters.
  2. Open Saved views.
  3. Type a name in Name for this query.
  4. Choose Save this filter as a query. You see, for example, "Saved the query “My week”."

A query saves the filter the list is running. While Filters has changes you haven't applied, Save this filter as a query waits and says "Apply filters first". Display isn't saved with a query.

To run a saved filter, choose its name. Saved views then shows, for example, "Running “My week”". Each query also has Rename, Up, Down and Delete.

"Your queries changed in another tab, so they were reloaded." means you changed them somewhere else. Try again.

Columns

  1. Choose Columns.
  2. Tick or untick the columns under Show these columns.

The Hub keeps your choice for next time. Activity Id always shows. At first, HQ Tags, Lead Ministry, Status and Translations are hidden.

Month and Week

Choose Month or Week to see the same filter as a calendar. An activity that runs several days shows on each of them. Use Previous month, Today and Next month (or Previous week and Next week) to move. Choose List to go back.

At most 1,000 activities fit. "Only the first 1,000 activities are shown. Narrow the filter to see the rest." means there are more.

Watch an activity

Choose the star beside an activity to add it to your watchlist. Choose it again to remove it. Point at the star to see who else watches it, or "Nobody watches this yet".

Use My Watchlist Only in Filters to list your starred activities. The star also works during the daily change freeze.

Excel export

  1. Choose Export and reports. Check the filter it says it will use, such as "Uses your list filter: none (every activity you can see)."
  2. Choose Excel export. A spreadsheet of the activities your filter finds downloads, up to 10,000.
Message What it means
"More than 10,000 activities match: narrow the filter and export again" Narrow the dates or the filter.
"Other exports are running: try again in a few seconds" Wait a moment and try again.

For the PDF reports in the same panel, see Reports.

The freeze line

"Daily change freeze." at the top of the list says when no changes can be made. While the freeze applies to you, it shows as a Change freeze warning and New activity is hidden. See The edit lock and the daily change freeze.

Older activities

Activities that ended before the move to this Calendar weren't brought over, except awareness dates. If you need an older one, ask a Calendar administrator.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"From must be on or before To." Fix the dates.
"No activities match." Nothing fits the filter. Widen it, or choose Reset.
"(no longer available)" in a filter box The filter names a choice that was removed. Choose another.
"Couldn't save your list settings." Your column or display choice wasn't kept. Try again.

calendar-editor-updates.html:
Who this is for: Calendar editors (Calendar.Editor).

Calendar > Updates lists recent changes to the activities you can see, newest first. It opens on Today's updates. Latest 5 updates shows the five newest.

Each line says when, who, and what they did: "added activity", "changed activity", "reviewed activity" or "added new clone". Then come the activity's number, its title and its dates as they are now. Point at the title to see the summary.

Choose the activity's number to open it. Save or Cancel there brings you back to the same updates.

Find older updates

  1. Fill in From and To. From starts at yesterday. Both days are included. Leave either one empty to leave that end open.
  2. To narrow it, choose an Update type: Changed, Added, Deleted, Reviewed or Cloned. Deleted finds nothing for you, since you can't see deleted activities.
  3. To narrow it further, type in Search for: words in the activity's title or summary, or the name of who made the change.
  4. Choose Search.

To see one activity's updates, type its number above 10,000, such as HLTH-20001, in Search for. Shorter numbers, and words like COVID-19, are searched as text.

At most 1,000 updates show at once. "Showing the newest 1,000. Narrow the dates or the search to see older updates." means there were more.

What isn't here

  • Changes from before the new Calendar started. Open the activity and choose View changes: older changes are marked "from legacy log".
  • Transfers between comm contacts, and Clear LA Status. Those show only on the activity's View changes.
  • Activities you can no longer see. When an activity is marked Not for Look Ahead, moved to another ministry or deleted, its updates leave the list for anyone who can't see it now.
  • Changes to the Look Ahead fields, unless you see those fields. HQ editors see them; ministry editors don't.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"From must be on or before To." Fix the dates.
"No updates." Nothing changed in that time, or nothing matches the search.
"Activity not found: it doesn't exist, or you can't see it." Check the number.

calendar-editor-activity.html:
Who this is for: Calendar editors (Calendar.Editor).

You add activities for your ministries, and change the activities your ministries lead. As an HQ editor you can add and change any ministry's activities you can see. What each field is for is on Activity fields.

Add an activity

  1. On Calendar, choose New activity.
  2. Fill in the fields. The times start as 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM. If you have only one ministry, it is already the Lead Ministry. If you are a comm contact of the lead ministry, you are already its Comm Contact. Choosing another Lead Ministry picks you again where you are one of its comm contacts, until you choose a comm contact yourself. The End date follows the Start date until you set the end date yourself.
  3. Choose Save. You see, for example, "Created HLTH-21." The activity stays open, so you can add files.

New activity is hidden during the daily change freeze, unless you are an HQ editor.

Change an activity

  1. Open the activity: choose its title in the list or the calendar, or its number on Updates.
  2. Make your changes. As soon as you change something, the activity is yours to edit: anyone else who opens it sees it read-only until you finish.
  3. Choose Save. You are back where you came from and see, for example, "Saved HLTH-21."

Cancel goes back without saving. If you have unsaved changes, the Hub asks "You have unsaved changes to this activity. Leave anyway and discard them?" Choose Stay or Leave.

If Save finds a problem

A box at the top, "Fix these to save", lists each problem, such as "Enter a title" or "Choose a comm contact". Choose one to go to its field. Nothing is saved until they are fixed.

A start or end date in the past is only a warning: "The start date is in the past." or "The end date is in the past." The activity still saves.

What happens when you save

  • A new activity is New. Saving a change to most fields makes it Changed, until HQ reviews it.
  • HQ sees which fields changed, marked "Changed: needs review".
  • Everyone who can see the activity sees your change straight away, in the list, on Updates and in reports.
  • The change reaches Releases within a minute. A release already linked to the activity doesn't change. If a linked release is still to go out and you change a date or time, a warning above Save says so, for example "A release is planned against HLTH-21 (Release 2026HLTH0001: Scheduled, Nov 4, 2026 10:00 AM). Changing the date or time here doesn't move the release. Tell the release editor." The same words follow "Saved HLTH-21." Tell the release editor. See Releases and the Forecast.
  • Every change is kept in View changes.
  • Nobody is emailed. Tell people yourself if they need to know.

Activities you can only view

"Your ministry is shared on this activity: you can view it but not change it." means another ministry leads it. The fields are read-only, each checklist shows only what is ticked (or "None"), and the button is Back.

An activity also opens read-only while someone else is editing it, or during the daily change freeze. See The edit lock and the daily change freeze.

Clone an activity

Clone opens New activity filled in from this one, for the same lead ministry and comm contact. Nothing is created until you choose Save.

  1. Open the activity.
  2. Choose Clone. New activity opens with "This is an unsaved copy of HLTH-21. Nothing is created until you choose Save. Cancel leaves no copy behind."
  3. Change what differs, and choose Save. You see, for example, "Cloned HLTH-21 as HLTH-22." The new activity stays open, so you can add files.

Cancel, or leaving the page another way, creates nothing.

The copy starts as New, and its View changes says "created it as a clone", naming the activity it was cloned from. Like any new activity, the copy must have every required field filled in before it saves; an older activity may be missing some. It copies the activity's fields except these:

  • the release date and time are emptied;
  • Internal notes is emptied;
  • News Subscribe is emptied;
  • of the HQ Tags, only "30-60-90" is kept;
  • files and linked releases stay with the original.

If you have unsaved changes, Clone waits: "Save or cancel your changes to review or clone." Clone isn't offered during the daily change freeze, unless you are an HQ editor.

Add files

The Records section appears only when it is turned on for your Calendar. When it shows:

  1. Save a new activity first. Until then it says "Save the activity first to add files."
  2. Under Records, choose Add files and pick one or more files.
  3. Each file is added straight away, on its own. You see, for example, "Added 2 files."

A file can be a PDF, a PNG, JPEG or GIF image, a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file, an Outlook message, RTF, text or CSV. Each can be up to 25 MB, and an activity holds up to 50.

A file with the same name as one already attached replaces it, but only after you agree. The Hub asks, for example, "A file named Briefing note.docx is already attached (added Oct 12, 2026 by Pat Smith). Replace it? The old file is deleted." Choose Replace, and you see "Replaced Briefing note.docx." Choose Cancel, and you see "Nothing was added.": none of the files you picked is added.

To remove a file, choose Remove beside it, then Remove again in the "The file is deleted from this activity." box.

Adding or removing a file doesn't touch your unsaved changes to the fields. Like saving, it isn't possible while someone else is editing the activity, or during the daily change freeze unless you are an HQ editor. A file opens only for people who can see its activity.

View changes

View changes lists every change to the activity, newest first. Each entry says when, who and what they did, such as "created it", "changed it", "created it as a clone" (the copy may have been changed before it was saved), "reviewed it", "transferred it" or "cleared its LA status". A table shows each field before and after. Changes brought over from the old Calendar are marked "from legacy log".

Choose Back to the activity to return.

Delete an activity

You can't delete activities, so Delete isn't offered. Ask a Calendar administrator of the lead ministry, or an HQ administrator.

If your session runs out

If you are signed out while you have unsaved changes, sign in again and open the same activity. It says "Your unsaved changes were restored." Signing out yourself discards them.

Can't do this?

Message What it means
"It doesn't exist, or you can't see it." (under "Activity not found") Check the number. The activity may be led by a ministry you're not in, or it was deleted.
"Someone else changed this activity — reload to see their changes" Someone saved it, reviewed it or cleared its LA status after you opened it. Choose Reload. If you have unsaved changes, it asks "Reload and lose your changes? The activity as it is now replaces them." Choose Reload, then make your change again, or Keep editing.
"This activity is no longer available." It was deleted, or moved out of your ministries, after you opened it.
"This activity is deleted" Someone deleted it while you were editing. Your changes stay on the page but can't be saved.
"You can only choose one of your ministries" Choose one of your own ministries as the Lead Ministry.
"Choose a comm contact of the lead ministry" The comm contact belongs to another ministry. Choose another.
"That comm contact is no longer active" or "That person's account is inactive" Choose another comm contact. An activity that already has them still saves, but can't be cloned.
"That category is no longer in use" Choose another category.
"You can no longer copy the activity this was copied from. Start a new activity instead." The activity you cloned was deleted, or moved out of your ministries, while the copy was open. Choose Cancel, then New activity.
"Couldn't save. Your changes are still here; try again." Something went wrong on the way. Choose Save again.

calendar-editor-fields.html:
Who this is for: Calendar editors (Calendar.Editor).
