An activity's fields are in sections, in this order: Overview, Ministry, Planning, Schedule, Release, Event and, when turned on, Records. HQ editors also see Look Ahead, after Event. A "?" beside a field explains it.

What you must fill in

Fields marked "(required)" must be filled in before you can save:

  • Category, Title, Lead Ministry and Comm Contact;
  • Start date and End date, and both times unless you tick All Day;
  • Summary, Significance and Scheduling considerations. For HQ editors these three are optional.

A category that is a release, such as Approved Release, also needs Origin, Distribution and at least one Comm Materials. The message says, for example, "Choose the origin: this category is a release".

Overview

Field What to enter
Category The kind of activity. HQ Placeholder is offered only to HQ editors.
Confidential (not for Look Ahead) Tick it to make the activity confidential. The old Calendar called it Not for Look Ahead. Only its lead and shared ministries, HQ advanced users and HQ administrators then see it, and it isn't offered on the releases Forecast. A new activity isn't given a Look Ahead section, but ticking it doesn't take away a section the activity already has.
Title Up to 100 characters.
Summary Up to 700 characters.
Issue Tick it if the activity is an issue.
Significance Why it matters. Up to 500 characters.
Lead Organization The organization leading it, when that isn't the lead ministry, such as a partner. Up to 80 characters.
HQ Initiatives & Leads Tick the initiatives it supports.
HQ Tags Type a tag and choose Add tag, or press Enter. Existing tags are suggested as you type. A new tag is created when you save. Up to 20. Choose × beside a tag to remove it.

Ministry

Field What to enter
Lead Ministry One of your ministries. In an HQ organization, any active ministry. Some ministries can't lead activities and aren't offered. Changing it empties Comm Contact if the contact belongs to another ministry.
Cross-Government Tick it for a cross-government activity. It doesn't change who sees the activity.
Shared With Tick the other ministries that should see it. They can open it but not change it.

Planning

Field What to enter
Comm Contact The communications person responsible. Only the active comm contacts of the Lead Ministry, chosen above, are offered.
Key activity Tick it for a key activity.
Strategy Up to 500 characters.
Comm Materials The products planned, such as a news release.
Internal notes Up to 4,000 characters.

Schedule

Field What to enter
All Day Tick it for an all-day activity. It hides the times below it.
Dates Confirmed Tick it once the date is firm. Only confirmed activities are offered on the releases Forecast.
Start date, Start time Times go in 5-minute steps.
End date, End time The end can't be before the start.
Potential Dates A general timeline, like "late June". No numbers, TBC or TBD. Up to 50 characters.
Scheduling considerations Anything that affects the timing. Up to 500 characters.

Release

Some categories, such as TV / Radio and Awareness Day / Week / Month, have no release. For those this section is hidden, and choosing one empties the release date and time.

Field What to enter
Release date, Release time When the news release goes out. Fill in both, or leave both empty: Release time starts at "Choose a time". It can't be after the end date.
Origin, Distribution Where the release comes from, and how widely it goes.
Translations Required The languages needed.
Sectors, Themes, News Subscribe The release's topics. A release editor can copy them into a release.
BC Gov News The news releases linked to this activity. See Releases and the Forecast.

Event

Field What to enter
Premier Requested Whether the Premier was asked to take part, such as Yes, No or Invited.
Representative Who represents government at the activity.
At BC Legislature Tick it if it takes place there.
City, Venue Where it takes place. When you choose the city for places not on the list, Other City appears: type the city there. Venue and Other City take up to 55 characters.
Event Planner, Digital Who plans the event, and the videographer.

Look Ahead

Only HQ editors and above see this section. When a ministry editor saves, it stays as it is.

Field What to enter
Executive Summary Shown in HQ's Look Ahead report. Up to 2,000 characters.
LA Status None, New or Changed. HQ's Look Ahead flags the activity NEW or CHANGED.
LA Section Where the activity goes in the Look Ahead. It is worked out from fields above it: Category, Issue, Confidential (not for Look Ahead), Lead Ministry, Comm Materials, Dates Confirmed and the start and end dates. Its hint names them. Choose another section to override it; it then says "Override" and offers Use the inferred section. Awareness dates and activities led by the ministry shown as CITENG keep a fixed section, which can't be overridden.
Long Term Outlook Tick it to list the activity in the Look Ahead's Long Term Outlook.

A clone's Executive Summary is set to "**".

An activity marked Confidential (not for Look Ahead) whose section is overridden needs an Executive Summary.

For Records, see Add or change an activity.

Choices no longer in use

A choice that has been retired shows "(no longer in use)" when an activity already has it. The activity keeps it. You can't choose it for another activity.

Long text from the old Calendar

Some activities brought over from the old Calendar have longer text than the limits allow. They still save. The limits apply only to text you change.

calendar-editor-lock-and-freeze.html:
Who this is for: Calendar editors (Calendar.Editor).

Two things can open an activity read-only even though you may change it: someone else editing it, and the daily change freeze.

When someone else is editing

Only one person edits an activity at a time. The first person to change a field holds the edit lock. Anyone else who opens the activity sees, for example, "Pat Example is editing this activity (since 2:15 PM). It opens for editing when they save or cancel, or after 15 minutes without input."

The page stays read-only. It opens for you by itself, without a reload, once they save, cancel or leave it alone for 15 minutes.

When your lock lapses

If you leave the page alone for 15 minutes, your lock lapses and you see "Your edit lock lapsed. Save will work only if no one else has taken it or changed the activity." Your changes stay on the page. Choose Save: it works if nobody else changed the activity. If someone did, you are asked to reload.

When it is open in another tab

"You're editing this activity in another tab." means you are editing it in another tab or window. Choose Continue here to edit it in this one instead.

The daily change freeze

Every day from 4pm to 5pm BC time, only HQ can make changes. The list and each activity show "You cannot make content changes between 4pm-5pm. Contact the Corp Cal Manager to have emerging or urgent updates made for you during this time."

During the freeze, unless you are in an HQ organization:

  • New activity is hidden.
  • Activities open read-only, with a Change freeze warning.
  • Clone isn't offered, and files can't be added or removed.
  • A save you started before 4pm and send after 4pm is refused with the same message. Your changes stay on the page. Save again at 5pm.

These still work during the freeze: the list, filters, My Queries, the star, Updates, View changes, the Excel export and the reports.

For an urgent change during the freeze, contact the Corp Cal Manager at GCPE HQ.

If you are an HQ editor, the freeze doesn't apply to you. You see the times on the list, but you can keep working.

calendar-editor-hq.html:
Who this is for: Calendar editors (Calendar.Editor) who belong to an HQ organization, such as GCPE Headquarters.

If none of your ministries is an HQ organization, nothing on this page applies to you.

What HQ editors can do that ministry editors can't

With nothing to clear, you see, for example, "No activities up to 8 days ahead have an LA status to clear."

new-government.html:
Who this is for: Core administrators (Core.Admin), with one part for site editors (NRMS.SiteEditor).

The Hub dates the archive, builds its pages and sends old ministry addresses to the new ones by itself. You enter one date and, where ministries change, prepare one cabinet change.

At a glance

When Who What to do
The swearing-in date is announced Core administrator Government terms > Start new government term, and enter the date.
Before the swearing-in Core administrator Organizations > Cabinet change: add the renames, new ministries and hand-overs, preview them, then schedule them for the swearing-in time.
Swearing-in day Nobody The term changes over at midnight Pacific. A scheduled cabinet change publishes by itself.
After the swearing-in Site editors Minister photos and biographies on Organizations, and the banner on Website > Site settings > Site banner. Update minister contact records in Media Hub by hand.

1. Start the new term

Core administrators only.

  1. Open Government terms and choose Start new government term.
  2. Enter the Start date (required), normally the swearing-in date, and choose Continue.
  3. Read the dates in the question, then choose Confirm.

The start date decides where every release is listed in the public archive: releases published from that day are listed under the new term. You can fix a wrong date later with Edit. The Government terms page of the Core administrator manual has the details.

2. Prepare the ministry changes

Core administrators only.

  1. Open Organizations and choose the Cabinet change link.
  2. Add each change: Rename or change a ministry, Add a new ministry or Hand over a ministry. To merge ministries, add the new ministry first, then hand each old one over to it.
  3. Choose Preview and fix anything listed under "Fix these before publishing".
  4. Choose Schedule…, enter the swearing-in date and time (BC time), and choose Schedule.

Nothing changes for anyone until it publishes. The Cabinet change page of the Core administrator manual has the details. A single ministry can also be handed over on its own from Organizations, as its Organizations page explains.

3. On the day

Nobody needs to do anything.

  • At midnight Pacific on the start date, the public archive gets a page for the new term and its current-term link points there.
  • At the scheduled time, the cabinet change publishes: all of it or none of it. The public Ministries page updates within a few minutes. Old ministry addresses send visitors to their successors. Subscribers, staff, Calendar activities and draft releases move shortly after.
  • If the cabinet change can't publish, it goes back to a draft. Cabinet change shows "This change wasn't published" with the reason. Nothing is half done: fix it and publish it.

4. After the swearing-in: site editors

  1. On Organizations, choose Edit on each ministry and update the Minister name, Minister photo URL and Minister biography. Upload photos under Website > Files first. See Organizations.
  2. Take down or change any election notice on Website > Site settings > Site banner, and publish. See Site banner.
  3. Update the ministers' contact records in Media Hub. The Hub does not change them.

signing-in-and-unsaved-changes.html:
Who this is for: Everyone who uses the Hub.

Staying signed in

While a Hub tab is open, it keeps you signed in, even when the tab sits behind other windows. Your session can still end: when you sign out in another tab or window, when your computer has been asleep or offline for a while (it can be as little as a few minutes, and is never more than an hour), when the browser has put a tab it hasn't shown for a long time to sleep, or when an administrator changes your account.

When your session ends

If the screen you are on has nothing unsaved, the Hub goes to the sign-in page, which says "Your session ended. Sign in to carry on where you left off." Once you sign in, you are back where you were.

If the screen has unsaved changes, it stays as it was, and a box says "Your session has ended". Nothing can be saved until you sign in again: if you choose a button that saves, the screen says "Your session has ended. Sign in again to save — your changes are still here." and the box comes back.

  • Choose Sign in again to go to the sign-in page. Afterwards you come back to the same screen. Changes to a release's documents and to a Calendar activity are kept on this computer and come back, with "Your unsaved changes were restored." Other unsaved changes are lost.
  • Choose Stay on this page to copy what you need first. "Your session has ended" stays at the top of the page, with its own Sign in again.
  • Or sign in again in another tab. Come back to this tab and you can save as usual.

Leaving a screen with unsaved changes

On every screen where you change something, the Hub asks before you leave with changes you haven't saved: "You have unsaved changes on this page. Leave anyway and discard them?" This covers the side menu, links, Help and your browser's Back. Choose Stay to keep working, or Leave to discard the changes. Closing or reloading the tab gets your browser's own question.

Sign out asks too: "You have unsaved changes on this page. Sign out anyway and discard them?" Choose Stay, or Sign out to discard them. Signing out yourself also discards any changes the Hub kept on this computer.

If a screen can't be shown

If something goes wrong on a screen, you see "Something went wrong" and "This page couldn't be shown. Reload the page to try again." Choose Reload, or Go to the start page. The side menu still works. If it keeps happening, tell a Core administrator.

An address that doesn't lead to a screen shows "Page not found", with Go to the start page.
